title: Kevin Stefanski: We all trust in the process of Bijan Robinson's contract negotiations
summary: Falcons running back Bijan Robinson is not fully participating in training camp as he seeks a new contract.
full_text: Falcons running back Bijan Robinson is not fully participating in training camp as he seeks a new contract. Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski is not concerned about that. Asked about his own communications with Robinson, Stefanski declined to get into specifics, but he said he was confident that the two sides are doing everything they can. "I don't think it's fair to share those types of things," Stefanski said. "We all trust in the process of what's going on." Stefanski says he doesn't hold it against Robinson that he is choosing not to practice until he gets the contract he wants. "The NFL, you understand different things come up via all sorts of things, and contracts obviously are a part of that. It doesn't change relationships," Stefanski said. It is highly likely that the Falcons and Robinson will agree to a new deal before the season starts. Until then, Robinson will watch practice, and Stefanski sounds OK with that.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bears' Jaylon Johnson: Caleb Williams is the best quarterback I've had since Nick Foles
summary: Johnson may have damned Williams with faint praise in suggesting that Williams is not the Bears' best quarterback during Johnson's seven years in Chicago.
full_text: Chicago cornerback Jaylon Johnson has been with the Bears since they drafted him in 2020, and he's faced a lot of quarterbacks on the practice field during that time. Perhaps surprisingly, he doesn't necessarily view Caleb Williams as the best of those quarterbacks. In what might be considered damning with faint praise, Johnson talked up the Bears' offense when asked about training camp practices, but he suggested that Williams isn't the best Bears quarterback he's practiced against, just the best since Nick Foles was in Chicago during Johnson's first two seasons. "Honestly, this is probably the best offense I've had in seven years, as far as going against them, for sure. They've got a lot of speed," Johnson said. "Caleb's the best quarterback I've had, again, since I feel like maybe Nick Foles, if you want to go back that far. Just as far as slinging it, I feel like he's definitely doing his thing, you can see the accuracy, you can see the confidence, throwing the ball in tight windows is something that's stood out to me. Top to bottom they're a confident group. They believe in each other, believe in what they're doing. That's what we need to go against on defense. They know what we're doing, they challenge us, we go after them, it's going to be a fun camp." Foles had some stellar moments in his NFL career, making the Pro Bowl in his first season as the Eagles' primary starter in 2013, and winning Super Bowl MVP for the Eagles after the 2017 season. But that's not the Foles Johnson practiced against. Johnson was comparing Williams to the Foles who spent two years in Chicago late in his career, primarily as a backup to Mitchell Trubisky, Andy Dalton and Justin Fields. That makes it a strange comparison. The Bears only won three games started by Foles during his two seasons as Johnson's teammate. The Bears won 11 games in the regular season and one in the playoffs last year. That apparently isn't enough for Johnson to declare Williams the best quarterback he's practiced against in Chicago, without exception.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Aaron Rodgers credits his wife for mended fences with family
summary: The final season of football for Aaron Rodgers was preceded by a reunion with his estranged family.
full_text: '' The final season of football for Aaron Rodgers was preceded by a reunion with his estranged family . He spoke about it during a Saturday appearance on NFL Network. "There's been a lot of conversation about it outside of my own conversation for so many years," Rodgers told Kyle Brandt. "You know, a big part of it was getting married and having those conversations with my wife that allowed me to kind of open up to the possibility of coming together. It's been a couple-year process now, the conversations with them, but, you know, I've been very, very closed off about that part of my life, and I want to keep it that way. But there's been a narrative that's gone on for too long, that I wanted to kind of shut down. "And it's been really beautiful to reconnect with them. All of them. And I got to spend a week, a long weekend recently. Those pictures are from in Nashville. My parents, my brother, and his sweet wife, and their incredible two kids. I got to be an uncle. It's just really — it's really special. So a lot of my life has been full circle I think the last year. And that was part of it. I knew it was part of it. And I'm happy to be reunited, and that part of my life is a really beautiful addition, and I've got to give my wife a lot of credit for — not that she was pushing me, because she never was, but just the way that she loves and supports me, having her by my side during this process has been really special. And I missed those relationships. And there was reasons for it that don't need to be talked about, but I'm thankful that that's come all the way back around." Although Rodgers said he reconnected with "all of them," he mentioned only one brother. It's unclear whether Aaron and his brother, Jordan, have reconnected. It was Jordan who brought the family issues to light during a 2016 stint on The Bachelorette . Two years later, Jordan chided Aaron for his donation to wildfire-relief efforts after (per Jordan) Aaron didn't call their parents to check on them during the fires. Although it's good news when anyone finds a path back to the most important people in their lives, it's not entirely clear whether Rodgers truly wanted to reunite with his parents and at least one brother, or whether he simply wanted to "shut down" a "narrative." (Before anyone gets pissed at me for going there, those are the words he used.) Ian O'Connor's 2024 biography of Rodgers made abundantly clear his habit of cutting people close to him off by putting them on "the island." It will be interesting to see whether Jordan, who apparently is still marooned like Gilligan, will have anything to say about the latest developments.
author: Mike Florio

title: Deshaun Watson doesn't know why people think he doesn't like Cleveland
summary: Four years ago, when the Browns, Panthers, Falcons, and Saints entered a four-way competition for quarterback Deshaun Watson, Cleveland was the first team to which Watson said, "No thanks."
full_text: Four years ago, when the Browns, Panthers, Falcons, and Saints entered a four-way competition for quarterback Deshaun Watson, Cleveland was the first team to which Watson said, "No thanks." A five-year, fully-guaranteed contract quickly changed his mind. Still, there's been a lingering perception that Watson didn't really want to play for the Browns. Before too long, it seemed as if the Browns were counting the days until they could move on from Watson. Will that change? On Friday, owner Jimmy Haslam kept the door open on Watson returning in 2027. On Saturday, Watson made his feelings for Cleveland clear. "When I first got here, there was a lot of stuff going on, as the world knows," Watson told reporters. "But I don’t have any bad feelings toward Cleveland. I love Cleveland. Me and my wife have our house on the east side, so we’re here all the time. We were here this summer. If you ask around, I’m at pretty much all the restaurants, hanging out, so I haven’t had a bad experience outside of different times in the stadium. I don’t know why that narrative is out there that people think that I don’t like Cleveland. My family and I have been enjoying our time here, if the opportunity shows up, we’ll see where it goes.” The first step will be winning the starting job. The second step will be playing well enough to return. And the third step will be fending off any other teams that may want Watson, if he re-establishes himself as a high-level NFL starter.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyler Murray seems to be pulling ahead in Vikings QB competition, as expected
summary: In Murray vs. McCarthy, it seems inevitable that the newcomer will win the job.
full_text: We've been watching, but not saying much about, the drip-drip of the quarterback competition in Minnesota. Much of the evidence based on completion percentages and interceptions can be misleading, for various reasons. First, the quarterback of the starting offense will usually face the starting defense. The player running with the twos will be facing the second-string defense. Two, plays can be "scripted for success," aimed at making the player look better by dialing up a specific play against a defense the play is designed to beat. Three, it's not live football. The quarterback can't get hit. That introduces a real difference to the stress the player is feeling as the walls close in. That said, all online indications based on Saturday's practice are that Kyler Murray has begun to assert himself. Which makes sense. He's objectively more talented than J.J. McCarthy. If it was close at first, Murray's lack of knowledge and experience in the offense was a factor. Murray's speed and elusiveness have yet to move to the forefront. That gives him a clear advantage when it's time to play, since the threat of Murray running will keep defenses honest. Which could open up passing lanes that, in practice, defenses aren't going to abandon as quickly. The Vikings, who passed on keeping Sam Darnold and Daniel Jones a year ago in lieu of giving McCarthy a full season as QB1, didn't sign Murray to ride the bench. If he was going to be the backup, he likely would have cast his lot with the Rams, who wanted him to be the understudy to Matthew Stafford. Consider the comments of Vikings quarterbacks coach Josh McCown regarding the extra dynamic Murray brings to the position. "We've all seen SportsCenter , the stuff that he does with his legs — so you can’t discount that ," McCown said, via Jori Epstein of Yahoo Sports. "We want to coach him and kind of ask him, to a degree, to operate in our offense and then add his touch to it within that as those plays. The game gives you those opportunities. You don't know when it's going to happen, but those plays come up. And so we're hoping that that'll be a positive for us if/when that does happen. But it's coaching him as if he's just another Vikings quarterback that's in our system, learning our system, trying to grow him in our system the right way. And then again, letting his God-given ability and skill set take over when he plays." Through all of the clips and snippets and quotes and scorecards from the first week of camp, the one thing that resonates the most for us came from an unnamed Cardinals coach, who gave this candid and telling comment to Alec Lewis of The Athletic : "I think you're about to see the best version of Kyler Murray. And I'm fucking pissed that I'm not going to get to be a part of it. I'm going to be jealous when he's in a good environment, his headspace is good, and he shows people who the fuck he is." So, yes, it's a competition. But it would be a surprise if Murray doesn't win it. Especially since he brings to Minnesota's offense something it hasn't had since the days of Daunte Culpepper — a quarterback who is a real threat to tuck the ball and run to daylight.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys OLB Donovan Ezeiruaku expects more sacks than last season
summary: Cowboys outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku ranked in the top five among rookies in pressures, win rate, hits and hurries in 2025, according to Pro Football Focus.
full_text: Cowboys outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku ranked in the top five among rookies in pressures, win rate, hits and hurries in 2025, according to Pro Football Focus. Ezeiruaku, though, managed only two sacks. "They don't draft edge rushers to not get any sacks ," Ezeiruaku said, via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News . The Cowboys selected Ezeiruaku in the second round in 2025 after he led the nation with 16.5 sacks in his final college season at Boston College. Thus, last season wasn't what Ezeiruaku expected or wanted. "Especially for me, the way I take pride in what I do and what I want to do to help this football team," Ezeiruaku said. He is fully healthy now after undergoing offseason surgery for a hip injury he played through last season and ready to contribute more than he did as a rookie. "I feel very explosive," Ezeiruaku said.
author: Charean Williams

title: Andy Reid: Patrick Mahomes sure looks sharp out there
summary: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid continues to see positive signs from Patrick Mahomes in the quarterback's recovery from a torn ACL.
full_text: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid continues to see positive signs from Patrick Mahomes in the quarterback's recovery from a torn ACL. Reid said on Saturday that Mahomes has been doing a great job since training camp started. "He’s really doing everything that he normally does and doing it well. So, we’re happy with that," Reid told ESPN's Dan Graziano. "We know he’s still progressing through it. But he sure looks sharp out here ." Reid has continued to say that he's letting Kansas City's doctors and medical staff guide him when it comes to Mahomes' practice participation, if he'll play in a preseason game, and the quarterback's availability for Week 1. "As long as he’s safe, that’s what we’re looking at. So, right now, for what we’re doing, he’s safe to roll," Reid said. Reid has not said one way or another whether or not Mahomes will play in a preseason game. The Chiefs will host the Rams on Saturday, Aug. 15, play the Buccaneers on the road on Saturday, Aug. 22, and finish the preseason by hosting the Seahawks on Friday, Aug. 28.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Deebo Samuel on return to 49ers: "It kind of felt like I didn't even go nowhere"
summary: Samuel was back on the practice field with San Francisco on Saturday.
full_text: '' In the grand scheme of things, Deebo Samuel wasn't away from the 49ers for very long. Traded to the Commanders in March 2025, Samuel re-signed with the 49ers this week after just a one-year absence from the team that drafted him. "It kind of felt like I didn't even go nowhere, to be honest ," Samuel said Saturday after his first practice back with San Francisco, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "When I got back, I was just like, 'Well, I know what's going on, I know the people here. The staff's still the same.' So it's kind of like the same, for real. "They were happy, I was happy, and we're just ready to get the ball rolling.” While Samuel also has a history of requesting trades from the 49ers, he said there weren’t hard feelings with the team’s brass in head coach Kyle Shanahan and G.M. John Lynch. “Contract negotiations is contract negotiations, and then those are conversations for John, Kyle, and my agent to have," Samuel said. "But our relationship has never changed or had a fallout. So, that was just like contract negotiations that I'm not in control of.” Lynch told reporters on Saturday that Samuel will be used in a variety of roles in 2026, including returner and running back.
author: Myles Simmons

title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson diagnosed with a calf strain
summary: An MRI delivered good news to Bills safety C.J.
full_text: An MRI delivered good news to Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, who was carted to the locker room with a right leg injury during Saturday’s practice. He was diagnosed with a lower calf strain, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Gardner-Johnson will miss practice time but has six weeks until the season opener. The Bills signed Gardner-Johnson as a free agent this offseason. Gardner-Johnson, 28, played three games for the Texans and 10 for the Bears last season. He totaled 66 tackles, three sacks, four passes defensed and two interceptions in his 13 games. In his career, the seven-year veteran has recorded 370 tackles, 20 interceptions, 55 pass breakups and seven sacks.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bo Nix says his surgically repaired ankle won't hold him back
summary: Broncos quarterback Bo Nix is back practicing on his surgically repaired right ankle, which he fractured at the end of the divisional-round win over the Bills.
full_text: Broncos quarterback Bo Nix is back practicing on his surgically repaired right ankle, which he fractured at the end of the divisional-round win over the Bills. The third-year player said the injury will not change the way he plays. " Absolutely not ," Nix said, via Jeff Legwold of ESPN. "I'm going to roll [out]. I'm going to be as athletic as I can be. . . . It's a strength of ours and so we've got to use our strengths. For me that's when I feel at my best. That's when I feel free. When I'm playing like that, when I'm moving around, it's a good thing." Nix's 356 rushing yards last season were third on the team, and his five rushing touchdowns were second. He was sacked only 22 times despite 612 pass attempts. Coach Sean Payton has called Nix's mobility as "one of his superpowers." "It's hard to sack some quarterbacks, and he's one of them," Payton said after Saturday's practice. "That was something we saw on college tape and in our league, when you take a sack, just do the analytics on it, getting points on that drive or likelihood to kick a field goal, it all drops dramatically." Nix underwent two surgeries on his ankle, with the second a follow-up in April to treat bone spurs. He missed most of the team's offseason program but has no limitations in training camp. "I feel great, feel normal. Nothing's holding me back out there," Nix said. "Playing like I normally do, and I feel really good and continue to push and progress and also continue to get ready for this long season."
author: Charean Williams

title: Seahawks sign LB Joseph Vaughn
summary: The Seahawks added depth at linebacker on Saturday by signing Joseph Vaughn, the team announced.
full_text: The Seahawks added depth at linebacker on Saturday by signing Joseph Vaughn, the team announced. In a corresponding move, the Seahawks waived linebacker Ja'Markis Weston with an injury designation. Vaughn went undrafted out of UCLA in 2025, signing with the Colts. He spent camp with Indianapolis before the team waived him before the start of the season. The Colts signed him to a futures contract after the season but waived him this spring. In 2024 at UCLA, Vaughn appeared in 12 games in his one season with the Bruins. He totaled eight tackles. Before his time in Los Angeles, Vaughn played three seasons at Yale. He was a two-time All-Ivy League selection, including first-team honors in 2023. Weston, who signed to the Seahawks' practice squad late last season, would revert to Seattle's injured reserve list if he clears waivers.
author: Charean Williams

title: WR Deebo Samuel will also play running back and return kicks in second 49ers stint
summary: Receiver Deebo Samuel is officially back with the 49ers, for a second time.
full_text: '' Receiver Deebo Samuel is officially back with the 49ers, for a second time. And the 49ers won't be holding him back when it's time to play. On Saturday, G.M. John Lynch told reporters that Samuel will wear multiple hats during games. “You are going to see him in the return game, at receiver, and at running back ," Lynch said, via David Lombardi of the San Francisco Chronicle . "We are going to use him all over the field, and we are really excited to have Deebo back. We have a lot of history with him, we know the type of player he is, and he looks to be in really good shape.” Samuel became more involved in the running game in 2021, with 59 carries for 365 yards and eight touchdowns. Coupled with his 1,405 receiving yards and six touchdowns, it made him a first-team All-Pro. He had 42 carries in 2022, 37 in 2023, and 42 in 2024. Last year with the Commanders, he ran the ball 17 times for 75 yards. Samuel returned a decent number of kicks in the past two seasons. In 2024 with the 49ers, he had 17 kickoff returns for 533 yards, an average of 31.4 yards per return. In 2025 with the Commanders, he returned 15 kickoffs for 452 yards (30.1 yards). The more times any player touches the ball, the greater the risk of injury. And Samuel has a habit of fighting for every blade of grass, at all times. But Samuel has been largely durable throughout his career. And the 49ers will need him to make an impact on the offense, especially with Ricky Pearsall done for the year, Jauan Jennings gone via free agency, and Brandon Aiyuk stuck in a state of limbo that surely won't result in him returning to the 49ers roster.
author: Mike Florio

title: Stephen Jones: Cowboys wouldn't rule out selling a piece of the team
summary: Plenty of NFL owners have sold pieces of their teams, either to individual partners or to pre-approved private equity funds.
full_text: Plenty of NFL owners have sold pieces of their teams, either to individual partners or to pre-approved private equity funds. The Cowboys haven't, but they also won't close the door on it. " We wouldn’t rule it out , but, you know, we'd also be very particular in who we would bring in as a partner in terms of that," Cowboys executive Stephen Jones told 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Friday. "But, yes, it was designed when we passed that rule that you could have, you know, private equity involved in the NFL, and you could have minority partners, you know, it made sense for a lot of different reasons, and every owner who chooses to go that path can speak for themselves in terms of why they're doing it, but it does — I think it's a great tool. I think it makes the league stronger personally, and, certainly, it's not something we would ever totally rule out. But I wouldn't say anything's on the front burner, either." The valuation would surely be massive. They could possibly make upwards of $1.5 billion for only 10 percent of the team. And it wouldn't change anything about their control of the organization. But it also would result in 10 percent of the future profits going to the partner. Depending on how much the Cowboys are clearing after all expenses, it could be better over the long haul to retain all of the equity — and to keep all of the profits. Then there's the reality that equity typically has a greater value when it comes with control. Whatever the valuation on a limited slice of ownership, the full team would be worth more. And here's the basic reality. If the Joneses don't need the money, why sell any of the equity? Once it's gone, it's gone for good. (Unless they buy it back.) If business in Big D is truly booming, which we'll never know for sure without seeing the books, there's no reason to convert equity into cash.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaylon Johnson: 2026 is definitely a contract year for me
summary: Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson has two more years on his current deal, but he's looking at things a bit differently.
full_text: Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson has two more years on his current deal, but he's looking at things a bit differently. Johnson has no guaranteed money to go with a $25 million cap hit in 2027 and said that the coming season "is definitely a contract year" in his eyes. That comes after a 2025 campaign that was marred by a groin injury that cost Johnson 10 games. Framing this season as a push for a new deal "whether that’s here, somewhere else" means that Johnson will have to show he's back to top form in the wake of his injury troubles. "I'm not a dummy ," Johnson said, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com. "We all know that and I've structured my deal a certain way to put myself back at the table at the age of 27. For me, it was always for this point to get here, and then show how I do what I do and be healthy and be out there doing what I do best and that's covering, that's making plays, being a difference-maker. From there, wherever that contract talk goes, it goes." That's not exact motivation Bears head coach Ben Johnson was talking about in reference to his team managing hype this season, but it'll work if it means Johnson is back to being an effective corner for the entire season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Deshaun Watson: Preseason games great opportunity to showcase what I can do
summary: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson said on Saturday that his performance in training camp thus far has "been decent" and that he has his eyes on the next steps in his push to win the starting job in Cleveland.
full_text: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson said on Saturday that his performance in training camp thus far has "been decent" and that he has his eyes on the next steps in his push to win the starting job in Cleveland. The team will hold its first practice in pads on Monday and that will bring Watson closer to being in a game for the first time since tearing his Achilles midway through the 2024 season. Watson tore the Achilles again while rehabbing and he told reporters that he's eager for a chance to show how far he's come when the team starts playing preseason games. “I’m looking forward to it," Watson said, via a transcript from the team. "I haven’t played football in a long time, so for me, it doesn’t matter how long I play or how many games I play, I just want to play football. A lot of people wrote me off and said I wouldn’t be playing football again after two Achilles injuries. I’m proving that wrong and proving myself right. It’s a great opportunity for me to get out there and showcase what I can do.” Watson said he has no idea when head coach Todd Monken will make a call about who starts in Week 1 between him and Shedeur Sanders, which could make their preseason results a major factor in how things play out in Cleveland.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers rookie DE Mikail Kamara carted off practice field with apparent knee injury
summary: San Francisco 49ers rookie defensive end Mikail Kamara was carted off the practice field at training camp today.
full_text: '' San Francisco 49ers rookie defensive end Mikail Kamara was carted off the practice field at training camp today. Reporters on the scene said Kamara appeared to suffer a knee injury. Kamara was an undrafted free agent out of Indiana, where he was named Defensive Player of the Game in last season's College Football Playoff National Championship Game. Kamara played a total of six years for coach Curt Cignetti, four at James Madison and two more after transferring to Indiana when Cignetti became the Hoosiers' head coach. The 49ers were expecting Kamara to compete for a roster spot as a pass rusher and special teams contributor.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Lions agree to terms with LB Devin White
summary: The Lions have agreed to terms with free agent linebacker Devin White on a one-year deal, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report.
full_text: The Lions have agreed to terms with free agent linebacker Devin White on a one-year deal, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report. White, 28, is entering his eighth season. He spent last season with the Raiders and started all 17 games, totaling 174 tackles, 2.5 sacks, seven quarterback hits, one interception, three forced fumbles and one pass breakup. It was the first time he played all 17 games since 2022. The Buccaneers made White the fifth overall choice in 2019, and he spent his first five seasons in Tampa. He earned Pro Bowl honors in 2021, a season after second-team All-Pro accolades. In the three games in the 2020 playoffs when the Bucs won the championship, White recorded two interceptions, two pass breakups and two fumble recoveries. He played seven games for the Texans in 2024 before going to the Raiders for the 2025 season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Reports: Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen day-to-day with shin bruise
summary: Chiefs rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen appears to have avoided a serious injury on Saturday.
full_text: Chiefs rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen appears to have avoided a serious injury on Saturday. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Allen has been diagnosed with a shin bruise. Sam McDowell of the Kansas City Star reports that the team considers him day-to-day . Allen had to be carted off the field after getting hurt, so the minor nature of the injury is good news for the rookie. Allen has made a strong early impression in training camp while seeing time with the first team and it sounds like he'll be able to get back to that role in the near future. The Chiefs also saw wide receiver Xavier Worthy leave Saturday's practice with a shoulder injury. There's been no further update on his condition.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos to evaluate bringing in Taysom Hill
summary: Hill and Broncos head coach Sean Payton have a lot of history together.
full_text: Taysom Hill won't be back with the Saints in 2026, but the versatile tight end could wind up reuniting with a former coach. Broncos head coach Sean Payton told Steve Wyche and Cynthia Frelund of NFL Media that the team will explore bringing in Hill. Hill saw his first NFL action while playing for Payton in New Orleans in 2017 and would go on to see time as a tight end, quarterback, kick returner and various other offensive roles during their time together. Hill remained with the Saints after Payton left following the 2021 season, but said last week that " returning to New Orleans is not in the cards" this year. Given the history between Hill and Payton, the Broncos were seen as a possible next stop for Hill and that possibility feels a little more likely with the team set to consider the move.
author: Josh Alper

title: Will Levis: I know for sure I'm one of the 32 best quarterbacks in the NFL
summary: Titans quarterback Will Levis is competing with Mitch Trubisky to be the backup to Cam Ward.
full_text: '' Titans quarterback Will Levis is competing with Mitch Trubisky to be the backup to Cam Ward. But Levis thinks he should be a starter, somewhere. "There are not 32 quarterbacks in this league better than me," Levis said. "I know that for sure." Levis, the 2023 second-round pick who started 21 games in his first two seasons with the Titans but did not play at all last year, said he can take pride in what he's already done and thinks he'll get better. "I have more confidence than I've ever had," Levis said. "I know from the tape I've put on already that I'm a dang good quarterback in this league, even better than I ever have been." Levis said he is a more mature player now and less concerned about criticism or public perceptions of him. "This is really Year Four, I'm a true vet at this point," Levis said. "I've definitely grown a lot. I feel like I was a kid when I got here, now I'm a man."
author: Michael David Smith

title: As to the Browns' 5.5-win over-under, owner Jimmy Haslam would "take the over"
summary: There was a time, not all that long ago, when even a vague reference to betting lines by a broadcaster would sound every alarm at 345 Park Avenue.
full_text: ' There was a time, not all that long ago, when even a vague reference to betting lines by a broadcaster would sound every alarm at 345 Park Avenue. Times have definitely changed. Asked by reporters on Friday what a successful season would look like in 2026, owner Jimmy Haslam went straight to the wagering angle. “I would say this, and we never do this, but I think the odds are for us to win five and a half games," Haslam said. "I’ll take the over.” After going winless in 2017, the Browns went six straight seasons with six or more wins, including a pair of playoff appearances. Over the last two years, however, the Browns were 8-24. "We want to be fun to watch," Haslam said. "We want to play hard and not make mistakes. Look like we’ve got our act together, which is something we didn’t have the last two years, and the expectations are we will this year.” He said the team's overall struggles are "something that keeps us awake at night." "It’s unacceptable, and I hate it most for our fans, because they deserve better than that," Haslam said. "We’re working hard every day to not have that same kind of performance we’ve had in the past. We don’t have our heads in the sand — we know we haven’t performed.” They haven't. But they're not far from being competitive. This season could be a struggle with a new coaching staff and a quarterback competition. They still seem to be laying the foundation to be better than they've been. Truth be told, they can't be much worse than they were in 2024 and 2025.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling out of practice with hamstring tightness
summary: The 49ers placed Ricky Pearsall on injured reserve Saturday and one of the players in position to help replace him on offense is out of practice with an injury.
full_text: '' The 49ers placed Ricky Pearsall on injured reserve Saturday and one of the players in position to help replace him on offense is out of practice with an injury. Rookie De'Zhaun Stribling is not practicing because of hamstring tightness. The 49ers said, via multiple reporters, that Stribling is not dealing with a strain. In addition to losing Pearsall with a PCL injury, the 49ers have been practicing without veteran Christian Kirk. Kirk has missed several days with a calf injury. Stribling was the first pick of the second round this year and his early work has earned rave reviews from quarterback Brock Purdy. A brief absence probably wouldn't alter plans for him to play a role right out of the gate, but any extended time off the field would work against an early impact for the rookie.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dave Toub explains presence of rookie WR Cyrus Allen on special teams at practice
summary: Promising Chiefs rookie receiver Cyrus Allen exited Saturday's practice on a cart.
full_text: Promising Chiefs rookie receiver Cyrus Allen exited Saturday’s practice on a cart. The injury happened while he was filling the role of gunner on the punt team. That has prompted some Chiefs fans to question why in the hell Cyrus Allen was serving as a gunner on the punt team. Chiefs special-teams coordinator Dave Toub addressed the issue in a post-practice press conference with reporters. “I hate to see somebody get hurt, especially on special teams," Toub said, via Nate Taylor of ESPN. "He’s doing well on offense and for me, too. He was a gunner and a returner. Everyone is on special teams until they aren’t. Everyone starts as a four-phase guy, especially rookies ." Toub added that first-round cornerback Mansoor Delane would also be practicing on special teams, but for his shoulder injury. Toub also said that, once upon a time, tight end Travis Kelce practiced on special teams. It's another example of the delicate balance of getting a football team ready for the season while keeping the individual players as healthy as possible. If too many players are kept in bubble wrap during August, it becomes difficult to compete in September.
author: Mike Florio

title: Xavier Worthy left Chiefs practice with a shoulder injury
summary: The Chiefs lost a pair of wide receivers to injuries at Saturday's training camp practice.
full_text: The Chiefs lost a pair of wide receivers to injuries at Saturday's training camp practice. Rookie Cyrus Allen was carted off with a lower left leg injury that the team said is still being evaluated and third-year wideout Xavier Worthy had to leave the session with a shoulder injury. The extent of that injury is also under evaluation. Worthy missed time early last season after dislocating his shoulder and finished the year with 42 catches for 532 yards and a touchdown. Wide receiver was already seen as a spot where the Chiefs might look to bolster the ranks ahead of the regular season. If either of Saturday's injuries lead to long-term absences, it will increase the urgency to make a move in Kansas City.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brandon Beane: C.J. Gardner-Johnson will have an MRI and we'll see
summary: Bills safety C.J.
full_text: Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson left Saturday's practice on a cart after suffering what appeared to be an injury to his lower right leg and there's no immediate word as to the severity of the injury. Gardner-Johnson was not contacted before the injury and got on the cart after a brief examination on the field. After the practice, General Manager Brandon Beane said that further word on his outlook would wait for testing. “I don’t know anything yet . Until we get an MRI, we’ll see," Beane said, via John Wawrow of the Associated Press. The Bills signed Gardner-Johnson as a free agent this offseason and he was set to play a big role in the team's secondary, so any bad news on the MRI will lead to some shuffling on the back end of the defense in Buffalo.
author: Josh Alper

title: Todd Bowles had no reaction to Baker Mayfield's contract comments
summary: On Thursday, Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield had plenty to say about his inability to get the team to offer him a contract that he deemed to be suitable.
full_text: On Thursday, Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield had plenty to say about his inability to get the team to offer him a contract that he deemed to be suitable. On Friday, coach Todd Bowles was asked for his reaction. "I didn't have a reaction," Bowles told reporters. "You know, he had a few things to say. He said it. We're all about ball today, and we moved on." Bowles has the kind of even keel that rarely results in him having a public reaction to anything — except when the team blew a Thursday night game against the Falcons. From Bowles's perspective, Mayfield's status beyond 2026 doesn't matter. With 10 head-coaching jobs opening up after the 2025 season, it's clearer than ever that the NFL is a year-to-year business. Mayfield's contract status gives him an added incentive to have the best year possible in 2026. Which will boost Bowles's prospects for returning in 2027.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals sign DL Brodric Martin
summary: The Cardinals made a change on their defensive line Saturday.
full_text: ' The Cardinals made a change on their defensive line Saturday. The team announced the signing of Brodric Martin. He will take the roster spot that opened up when the team placed defensive lineman P.J. Mustipher on injured reserve. Martin was a 2023 third-round pick of the Lions and he appeared in five games over two seasons with the team. He also played in one game for the Steelers last season. Martin had four tackles in those appearances. Mustipher injured his foot in practice and will not be eligible to return to the Cardinals during the regular season. He had 32 tackles in 15 games for Arizona last season.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers are putting WR Ricky Pearsall on season-ending IR
summary: 2024 first-rounder won't play in 2026, due to lingering PCL injury.
full_text: '' 49ers receiver Ricky Pearsall's third NFL season is already over. Via Matt Barrows of The Athletic, G.M. John Lynch said Saturday that the team will be putting Pearsall on injured reserve . By rule, he won't be eligible to return to the 49ers in 2026. Pearsall had a lingering PCL injury from 2025. He'll have surgery to repair the situation in the hopes of being healthy in 2027. A first-round pick in 2024, Pearsall's debut was delayed after he was shot during a robbery attempt on Labor Day weekend. He eventually appeared in 11 games, with four starts. Last year, he started all nine games in which he played. For his career, Pearsall has 67 catches for 928 yards and three touchdowns. On Thursday, the 49ers brought back receiver Deebo Samuel after he spent 2025 in Washington. They may need to add another receiver or two to complement veteran Mike Evans, who signed in March after 12 seasons in Tampa.
author: Mike Florio

title: Falcons extend guard Matthew Bergeron
summary: In his rookie year of 2023, Falcons guard Matthew Bergeron became an instant starter.
full_text: In his rookie year of 2023, Falcons guard Matthew Bergeron became an instant starter. With three years under his belt, he's now getting his reward. The Falcons have announced that Bergeron has been signed to a contract extension . ESPN reports that it's a four-year, $96 million deal, with $60 million guaranteed at least for injury. (The full guarantees at signing weren't specified.) Bergeron started all 17 games in 2023 and 2024. He started 15 games in 2025, missing two. As a rookie, Bergeron was on the field for every offensive snap. He was on track for free agency or the franchise tag in 2027. Now, he is signed through 2030. Next up, presumably, will be the team's first-round pick in 2023. The guy for whom Bergeron blocks. The guy who may be the best player in all of the NFL: running back Bijan Robinson.
author: Mike Florio

title: Patriots will activate rookie LB Gabe Jacas on Saturday
summary: It took a while to get his contract finished.
full_text: It took a while to get his contract finished. It took even longer to get him on the practice field, thanks to placement on the non-football injury list. On Saturday, rookie second-round linebacker Gabe Jacas will make his debut with the Patriots. "We’ll have Gabe back today," coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Saturday. "We’ll get Gabe back today. Get that out on social [media] here, guys. . . . He’ll be out there in a limited role. We’ve talked to you about the return to play protocol that we have, and so now he gets handed over to the coaches, and that’ll be in a limited role. He won’t be involved in the team reps, but hopefully Monday, we’ll see him back out there." It's clear that Jacas has been wanting to get to work. "He loves football," Vrabel said. "He’s been itching to get back. He texts me all the time. He texts me late at night, 'Hey, am I going to practice tomorrow?' I’m like, 'No, just like I told you at 6:30 last night or tonight that you’re not going to practice tomorrow. You don’t have to text me at 10:00 and ask again. The answer is still no, not yet.' You want that. You want guys that are looking for ways in as opposed to looking for ways out. I think he just wants to get out there, get acclimated and be with his teammates. That is all he wants to do. He just wants to play football." He'll now get to do it, even if the path was a strange one — punctuated by an unusual injury waiver that exempts his left knee from guarantees in 2027 and 2028.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL training camp injuries tracker: Latest updates on Ricky Pearsall, C.J. Gardner-Johnson and more
summary: Pearsall is set to undergo season-ending knee surgery while Gardner-Johnson was injured during Saturday's Bills practice
full_text:
NFL training camp is typically a time for optimism. Hope abounds that all the changes a team made during the offseason -- whether hiring a new coach, signing players in free agency, acquiring them via trade or selecting them in the draft -- will lead to a better season than the year before.
The one thing every team needs to avoid for that to happen, of course, is injuries. A major injury can derail plans for the entire year, especially if it happens to a key player. Alas, injuries happen every year, and it's important to keep track of who's hurt, when and how the injury happened, and how long they might be sidelined.
With that in mind, consider this your one-stop shop for all the injury news coming out of NFL training camps during July and August.
Pearsall is expected to undergo season-ending surgery on his ongoing PCL injury that has been an issue since last season. Niners general manager John Lynch said that Pearsall is expected to make a full recovery.
Allen, who had been enjoying a strong start to his first NFL camp, was carted off the field on Saturday after colliding with Kaiir Elam on a special teams drill. ESPN later reported that test conducted on Allen revealed a shin bruise. Nothing was torn or broke, so he appears to have dodged a bullet.
During Saturday's practice, Johnson went down and was unable to put any weight on his right leg as he was aided off the field. He was also seen clutching the area around his Achilles. Despite being carted to the locker room, ESPN reports that Gardner-Johnson merely suffered a lower calf strain, so he avoided any serious injury.
Johnson, 28, was enjoying a solid start to training camp. A seven-year veteran, Johnson's NFL accolades includes a Super Bowl win with the Eagles and leading the NFL in interceptions back in 2022.
Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski that Tagovailoa is working through an injury and will the early portions of training camp. With Tagovailoa sidelined, the Falcons have signed veteran backup Cooper Rush .
Regarding fellow quarterback Michael Penix's status, Stefanski recently said that he still hasn't been cleared for full team activities. Penix is still working his way back from a torn ACL that was sustained during Week 11 of the 2025 season.
The Panthers placed Scourton on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee on the first day of training camp . Scourton was reportedly in tears as he left the field, and his teammates came over to hug him as he exited.
Head coach Dave Canales said at the time that Scourton would undergo an MRI to determine the severity of the injury, and the results confirmed the second-year edge rusher had torn his ACL.
The Saints were hit with awful news on Wednesday as it appears that Bresee suffered a season-ending ACL tear during Wednesday's practice. A former first-round pick, Bresee has quietly become one of the NFL's best defensive linemen. The Saints will now look to try to find his replacement for the upcoming season.
The 2025 first-round pick's Wednesday practice came to an abrupt end after his leg buckled . Stewart -- who played in just eight games during his rookie season -- was carted off the field shortly after sustaining the injury. According to ESPN , Stewart suffered a hyperextended knee with no ligament damage, which seems like best-case scenario given the initial reporting around the injury.
While the initial plan was for Brazzell to recover without surgery, a second opinion determined that a procedure to repair the moderate LCL tear in his left knee is the best course of action, according to The Athletic . The surgery will force Brazzell to miss his entire rookie season, which is a much longer timeline than the eight weeks that was presented in the immediate wake of his injury. The LCL tear does not appear to be related to the knee issue the third-round pick dealt with leading up to training camp.
James is expected to miss time after he suffered a rib fracture during Monday's practice. The 49ers have yet to offer a timeline for his possible return.
Mustapha sat out Wednesday's practice as he is dealing with a hamstring strain. Like James, Mustapha's injury occurred during Monday's practice.
McNeill left Friday's practice with a neck injury suffered in a pile-up during 11-on-11 drills, according to the Detroit Free Press . The Lions are already shorthanded in the secondary and can scarcely use an injury up front. McNeil wasn't himself last season after returning from a torn ACL and it's not a great sign to see him banged up early in camp this year.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Broncos to explore adding Taysom Hill, reuniting versatile tight end with Sean Payton
summary: After announcing his departure from the Saints, the versatile weapon could reunite with his former head coach Sean Payton in Denver
full_text:
Taysom Hill established himself in the NFL as one of the league's more unique Swiss Army knives, largely thanks to Sean Payton deploying him in various facets during their shared time in New Orleans. When Hill recently announced that he would not be returning to the Saints in 2026 and will explore other options across the league, it didn't take long for folks to connect the dots to Denver for a possible reunion with Payton. And it seems like Payton is enamored with the idea himself, telling NFL Network that the Broncos will be exploring the possibility of adding Hill.
Hill, 35, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of BYU. After a brief stint with the Packers during training camp, he found his way to New Orleans and caught the eye of Payton. Under his tutelage, Hill was a versatile weapon as a passer, rusher and receiver, and had been listed as a quarterback, wide receiver and, more recently, a tight end.
Over the course of their tenure in New Orleans (2017-2021), Hill totaled 1,183 rushing yards and 16 rushing touchdowns, while catching 34 of his 47 targets for 388 yards and seven touchdowns. He also passed for 2,025 yards, eight touchdowns and eight interceptions, while completing 64.2% of his throws. Hill was 7-2 over his nine starts under center for the Saints.
"For the last nine years, New Orleans has been so much more than the city where I played," Hill said in his farewell post to the Saints . "It's where my family built a life, where our oldest son was born, and where we formed relationships and made memories that will stay with us forever. I've taken time this offseason to think carefully about what comes next for my family and me.
"I still don't have a clear answer about what the future holds, but I know that returning to New Orleans is not in the cards. As training camp begins, I didn't want my silence to be misinterpreted, and as hard as it is to put into words, I wanted to express my gratitude."
Of course, Bo Nix is the entrenched starting quarterback for Payton's Broncos, but the potential addition of Hill could help take some of the load off of him in obvious run situations, particularly as Nix continues to recover from a fractured ankle he suffered last postseason.
Moreover, he could help boost a tight end room that's currently headlined by Adam Trautman and Evan Engram . In 2025, those two accounted for 70 catches, 656 yards and just two touchdowns. In theory, Hill could help boost the position's touchdown output from a season ago if Denver elects to bring him aboard.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Ricky Pearsall injury: 49ers receiver to undergo season-ending surgery on lingering PCL
summary: Pearsall has been dealing with the issue since last season
full_text:
Injuries have hampered the 49ers for years, and that once again appears to be the case in 2026. On Saturday, the 49ers placed receiver and former first-round pick Ricky Pearsall on season-ending injured reserve. General manager John Lynch said that Pearsall will undergo season-ending surgery to address his nagging PCL injury that has bothered him since the 2025 season.
Lynch said that Pearsall will undergo surgery in the next couple of weeks. The timeline for Pearsall's recovery is six to 12 months.
Pearsall initially sustained the injury during the 49ers' loss to the Jaguars in Week 4 of the 2025 season. The injury led to Pearsall missing all or parts of 10 games.
Pearsall did not undergo surgery this offseason and, by all accounts, did not experience any major setbacks prior to the start of training camp, when he began to experience swelling in the knee.
"We reevaluated after [the season], and the consensus was that that [surgery] wasn't the step to take," Lynch said earlier this week, via ESPN . "He did well throughout the offseason, ran into some other road bumps. At that point between all the docs that we consulted ... the decision was made. As [team physician] Tim [McAdams] said, it's declared itself. And the course of action that everyone felt was appropriate was having surgery."
The 31st overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft , Pearsall's career so far has been marred by obstacles. Just before the start of his rookie season, Pearsall sustained a gunshot wound to the chest, which led to him being placed on the reserve/NFI list until Oct. 19. Pearsall caught 31 of 46 targets for 400 yards and three touchdowns that season.
Last year's knee injury limited Pearsall to nine games. He caught 36 of 53 targets for 528 yards. He caught one pass during San Francisco's season-ending loss to the Eagles in the NFC wild card round.
As noted above, the 49ers have dealt with a considerable amount of injuries over the years. Last season alone, the team dealt with significant injuries to several key players that included tight end George Kittle , linebacker Fred Warner , pass rusher Nick Bosa and quarterback Brock Purdy . The 49ers, desperate to find a solution to their injury issue, recently looked into whether or not excessive exposure to electromagnetic force (EMF) is contributing to the team's alarming injury rate.
Pearsall's injury coincides with the 49ers' officially re-signing former All-Pro wideout Deebo Samuel , who is back in San Francisco after spending the 2025 season with the Commanders . Samuel played a key role on the 49ers' NFC championship-winning squads in 2019 and 2023.
"Deebo has been, at times, one of the better players in football," Lynch said. "About a month ago we started having talks in earnest and came to fruition here a couple days ago, and we're thrilled to have him back."

full_text:
Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers aren't exactly on the best of terms entering the 2026 season. Mayfield recently went as far as saying he feels "disrespected" by the Buccaneers' contract offer, which allegedly did not extend beyond two years.
The Buccaneers reportedly offered Mayfield a two-year extension worth just north of $100 million, per ESPN , which also reported that the team isn't happy with how Mayfield has spoken about the organization in recent days. Clearly, the relationship between Mayfield and the Buccaneers is frayed.
While Mayfield will lead the Buccaneers' offense in 2026, his future with the team beyond that is very much in doubt. Mayfield has stressed that he wants to remain in Tampa, but he is currently slated to become a free agent after the 2026 season. Based on how contract talks unfolded, there's a good chance another team will make him an offer that makes him feel more valued than the Buccaneers have in recent months.
It's easy to see both sides. While Mayfield has enjoyed a career resurgence in Tampa, he still isn't considered an upper-echelon quarterback. He's just 28-26 as the Buccaneers' starting quarterback, including a 1-2 postseason record. A penchant for costly turnovers has often been Mayfield's Achilles heel.
That said, Mayfield has proven to be a productive starting quarterback who, at 31, should still have several solid seasons left. In the right situation, Mayfield -- who has won playoff games with both the Browns and Buccaneers -- has shown he's good enough to lead a team on a playoff run. If he plays well in 2026, he should have several offers to become another team's starting quarterback.
With that in mind, here's a look at six possible landing spots for Mayfield if he and the Buccaneers part ways after the 2026 season.
Arizona seems like the most realistic option for Mayfield if he becomes a free agent next offseason. The Cardinals currently don't have a long-term plan at quarterback and could use a player of Mayfield's stature to help turn things around.
The Cardinals will move forward this year with veteran backup Jacoby Brissett , but it seems clear they'll look to upgrade the position after the season. Mayfield would be a good fit for several reasons, starting with the fact that his experience and leadership could do wonders for a Cardinals team with promising young players like rookie running back Jeremiyah Love , tight end Trey McBride and wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr .
Atlanta makes sense for multiple reasons, starting with the fact that the Falcons don't have a stable situation at quarterback. Their current plan for 2026 involves Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. , but both are currently dealing with injuries, prompting Atlanta to sign veteran backup Cooper Rush at the start of training camp.
Mayfield took advantage of a favorable situation when he arrived in Tampa Bay, and he could be set up for similar success in Atlanta. The Falcons have one of the league's most impressive collections of skill players, including running back Bijan Robinson , wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts . Atlanta may be a quarterback away from becoming a serious contender.
Mayfield is also familiar with Kevin Stefanski after playing for him in Cleveland from 2020-21. During their first season together, Mayfield and Stefanski helped the Browns win the franchise's first playoff game since 1993. Their time in Cleveland didn't end well, however, and it appears there are still some ill feelings .
Houston is the only team in the NFL to win a playoff game in each of the past three seasons. C.J. Stroud's shortcomings over the past two years, however, are perhaps the biggest reason the Texans have yet to advance beyond the divisional round. They're also why Stroud hasn't received a long-term contract.
If Stroud doesn't take the next step this season, the Texans will undoubtedly be in the market for a quarterback in 2027. If that happens, it's easy to imagine Houston considering Mayfield, who would benefit from a solid supporting cast and arguably the NFL's best defense.
Another team that might be a quarterback away from serious contention. Like the Falcons, the Vikings are holding a quarterback competition between a veteran ( Kyler Murray ) and a recent first-round pick ( J.J. McCarthy ).
The odds are decent that the Vikings will be in the market for a quarterback in 2027. If that ends up being the case, it's safe to assume Minnesota will consider Mayfield, who could become the next former first-round pick to thrive under Kevin O'Connell. Like Atlanta, Minnesota has talented playmakers -- most notably Justin Jefferson -- who would increase Mayfield's chances of success.
The Jets are hoping Geno Smith can return to his Pro Bowl form, but if he can't, Gang Green could once again be looking for a quarterback in 2027. Given Smith's struggles with Las Vegas last season, there's a good chance the Jets will be in the market for quarterback help after the 2026 season.
Mayfield would be a clear upgrade over Smith, but it's safe to assume the Jets wouldn't be the first team on his wish list given their lack of success over the years. Still, if his options are limited, Mayfield may have to take whatever opportunity gives him a chance to start, which could lead him to New York.
Of all the teams on this list, the Steelers are the least likely to pursue Mayfield in 2027. Mike McCarthy is determined to find Pittsburgh's next franchise quarterback, and the Steelers currently have two promising young quarterbacks in Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar .
That said, Pittsburgh can't be ruled out because its 2026 starter, Aaron Rodgers , plans to retire after this season, and the Steelers don't have a proven quarterback behind him outside of Mason Rudolph , who has spent his career as a backup.
If nothing else, the Steelers could sign Mayfield to compete with either Howard or Allar. In that scenario, Pittsburgh probably wouldn't offer Mayfield a long-term contract, meaning he would have to bet on himself once again.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Betting the Ravens in 2026: See how Baltimore's win total, Super Bowl odds are trending and our best bets

For the first time since 2007, the Ravens will enter the 2026 season without John Harbaugh as head coach. Jesse Minter is now the fourth head coach in franchise history, with the last two winning Super Bowls during their tenures. That will be the expectation for Minter with perennial MVP candidate Lamar Jackson at quarterback. Harbaugh made the playoffs in 12 of his 18 seasons, so the new coach certainly has big shoes to fill.
We're taking a look at everything you need to know before making Baltimore Ravens futures bets below, including odds, trends, 2026 schedule, offseason changes and more before sharing our preseason betting strategy for the team. Odds are via DraftKings.

At -390, the Ravens are seen by the betting market as the biggest lock to make the playoffs in the AFC despite missing the postseason last year and transitioning to a new head coach. Only the Rams have lower odds to win the Super Bowl with Baltimore taking some steam during the offseason, and the Ravens are the favorites to win the AFC.
Perhaps the most surprising thing about the Ravens' 2025 season was finishing 6-7 in games started by Lamar Jackson, as the 2023 NFL MVP had a 70-24 record entering 2025. Expectations aren't any lower for the Ravens this year, with their projected win total sitting right around 11 based on how 10.5 and 11.5 are juiced. The last time the Ravens' win total was less than 10.5 was in 2018 when they blew by their 8.5 line in Lamar Jackson's first season as starter.

The Ravens' defense finished top nine in scoring in eight of the previous nine seasons heading into 2025, with Baltimore surrendering 37 points or more in four of its first five games and 24 or more in five of its last six. A good place for Minter to start focusing improvements is in the pass rush, where Ravens ranked 31st in sacks per pass attempt. The offense led the league in yards per rush but had major issues protecting the quarterback, ranking 29th in sacks per pass attempt.
The two areas of focus this offseason for the Ravens have been upgrading the interior of the offensive line as well as the edge rush. On offense, John Simpson returns after two years with the Jets, but the biggest addition was the draft's best pure guard prospect in Vega Ioane, and all that remains is figuring out how to replace Tyler Linderbaum at center. On defense, the team backed out of a Maxx Crosby deal due to a failed physical and instead signed Trey Hendrickson, who racked up 35 sacks over two seasons before missing the majority of 2025 due to injury. Second-round pick Zion Young brings additional juice to the edge rusher position.

The Ravens get to trade one of their road games for an international matchup, but that trip will mean a flight of 10-plus hours each way with no time off before or after the Week 3 game in Rio de Janeiro. On the plus side, the rest of the schedule doesn't involve too much travel with Houston their furthest destination, and a late bye should help reset for a playoff run provided the first 12 weeks aren't a disaster.

While Lamar Jackson is a cheat code, there are too many unknowns for me to get on board with the Ravens being the biggest playoff lock in the league and owners of one of the highest win totals. Declan Doyle is out from under Ben Johnson's shadow as offensive coordinator, and Minter will have to navigate the challenges of being a first-time head coach. The offensive line added a high-floor rookie but lost a key piece, while the defense also is in a spot of potentially losing more talent than it gained. It's easy to say that with good health the team should be a Super Bowl contender, but Jackson's 6-7 record and Ronnie Stanley staying healthy again last year during a down season suggest it's not that simple. The Ravens seem more like a 9-10 win team to me in the first year post-Harbaugh than one we should expect to challenge for the No. 1 seed.

title: Betting the Jets in 2026: See how New York's win total, Super Bowl odds are trending and our best bets

full_text:
The Jets finished in the bottom two of the AFC East for the 10th straight season in 2025 and they haven't made the playoffs since 2010, but management decided to give Aaron Glenn another year and a rebooted cast of characters to turn things around. With a new quarterback in Geno Smith, four rookies expected to contribute immediately in David Bailey, Kenyon Sadiq, Omar Cooper Jr. and DeAngelo Ponds, two new coordinators and nowhere to go but up, the Jets won't have to do much to beat the betting market's expectations for their 2026 season.
We're taking a look at everything you need to know before making New York Jets futures bets below, including odds, trends, 2026 schedule, offseason changes and more before sharing our preseason betting strategy for the team. All odds are via DraftKings.
Fans interested in betting on NFL and Super Bowl futures should check out the latest DraftKings promo code .
The Jets have seen steam to the Over on their win total thanks to what's perceived to be a strong offseason in terms of adding talent. While a trip to the postseason would still be a shocker, the Jets may be able to take advantage of a division with two new head coaches and potential regression from the AFC champions to get to at least six wins.
The Jets have gone Over the win total just twice since 2017 -- in 2022 as you can see in the table, and in 2017 when a Josh McCown-led squad had a win total of just 3.5 and finished 5-11. In the 10 years since the Jets have finished the season with a positive point differential, they've allowed 1,193 more points than they've scored, and only four teams had a lower point differential in 2025 than that 10-year average (including the Jets at a league-worst -203).

The Jets finished the season with the lowest pass yards per play mark in the league and topped 200 net passing yards in only five games while finishing with less than 60 net passing yards four times, including a brutal negative-10 net passing yards in a close loss to the Broncos. However, the offense did rank eighth in yards per rush, providing a positive to potentially build around. The lowlight on defense was becoming the first team to not record an interceptions since the NFL began tracking the stat back in 1933.
Whether the Jets will spark the passing attack this year should come down largely to two people: offensive coordinator Frank Reich and quarterback Geno Smith. When we last saw the former, he went 1-10 in Carolina before being fired, and the Panthers finished with the fewest passing yards in the league. Smith's success in Seattle did not carry over to Las Vegas, where he led the league in interceptions and times sacked in his one season with the Raiders. The pair will be supported by first-round draft picks at receiver and tight end, but not much else was done to upgrade the unit.
On the other hand, general manager Darren Mougey threw plenty of resources at the defense, with just four returning players expected to occupy starting positions. Key additions include the No. 2 overall pick David Bailey at edge rusher, T'Vondre Sweat on the defensive line, veteran Demario Davis at linebacker and Pro Bowler Nahshon Wright at corner.

My initial lean was to go Under the Jets win total, then I talked myself into making them the one positive play in this division. title: Betting the Patriots in 2026: See how New England's win total, Super Bowl odds are trending and our best bets

full_text:
After going 4-13 in Bill Belichick's final season in 2023 and repeating that record in Jerod Mayo's only season as head coach, a Patriots team led by Mike Vrabel pulled off one of the biggest turnarounds in recent history, adding 10 wins to their record while moving from -128 to +170 in point differential. The defending AFC champions will now look for similar success while playing a tougher schedule, and the road to a repeat starts with better protection in front of Drake Maye after the MVP candidate was battered by the elite Seahawks defense during the Super Bowl. One big piece of the puzzle shifted into place on June 1 with the acquisition of A.J. Brown from the Eagles.
We're taking a look at everything you need to know before making New England Patriots futures bets below, including odds, trends, 2026 schedule, offseason changes and more before sharing our preseason betting strategy for the team. Odds are via DraftKings.
Fans interested in betting on NFL and Super Bowl futures should check out the latest DraftKings promo code .
The Patriots were -150 to both go Over 9.5 wins and Under 10.5 wins on June 1, but while that price remained the same on the Over a month later, we saw a little movement on the 10.5. While they sit behind the Bills in divisional odds, the Brown trade did shorten the price by 5 cents initially, though the market threw some weight behind the Bills during July. The Patriots will have their shortest odds to win the Super Bowl in 2026 since Tom Brady left town.
A key trend to note for the Patriots in particular involves Super Bowl losers. Since the Patriots followed up their loss to the Eagles with a win over the Rams in Super Bowl 53 the following year, the seven Super Bowl losers have gone Over the win total the following season only once (Bengals in 2022), while three of the seven teams have won only six games, including each of the past two Super Bowl losers (Chiefs last year, 49ers the year before).

The Patriots' offensive success came largely from the passing attack, which finished tops in the league in yards per play by a significant margin and more than a full yard per play better than the fourth-ranked Bills. While the defense was well-balanced in defending the run and the pass, it ranked 30th in red-zone conversion rate and last in the league in goal-to-go situations, giving Mike Vrabel a key focus for improvement heading into 2026.
While finding a way to replace Stefon Diggs has been one focus of the offseason, perhaps nothing was more important than protecting Maye better up front. Vera-Tucker is a big-name addition on the interior, but his career has largely been defined by injury thus far, as he played 43 of 68 possible games during his four years with the Jets. The Patriots got their Diggs replacement in June by trading for A.J. Brown, who will pair with Romeo Doubs in an upgraded receiving corps. The other key addition was made in the draft by trading up for tackle Caleb Lomu.

If you're projecting a Super Bowl hangover, the miss playoff odds look to be a pretty good value unless you're also projecting a collapse from the Bills under their new regime. full_text:
With the Bills' run of five straight division titles ending in 2025 despite a seventh straight season with double-digit wins, Buffalo moves forward with a new head coach in Joe Brady and the same expectations to make it to a Super Bowl, something the Bills have failed to do every season since 1993 despite their recent success. Will a new coach, new defensive scheme and the same old MVP candidate at quarterback be enough to finally win the AFC?
We're taking a look at everything you need to know before making Buffalo Bills futures bets below, including odds, trends, 2026 schedule, offseason changes and more before sharing our preseason betting strategy for the team. Odds are via DraftKings.

The Bills were the co-favorites to win the AFC with the Ravens before A.J. Brown's trade to the Patriots put Buffalo slightly behind. The division is expected to come down to the Bills and Patriots, who are -340 to be the top two teams in the AFC East in some order when all is said and done. The Brown trade initially moved the division title line 5 cents, with the Bills dropping from -130, but the Bills' price regained that dip and then some by the start of August. While their Super Bowl odds have gotten a little shorter since February, their win total Over is a little bit cheaper to play heading into the preseason.
Since Josh Allen's first full season as QB1 in 2019, no team has scored more points than the Bills' 3,120, and no team has allowed fewer points than the Bills' 2,253. Buffalo's +957 point differential over the last seven seasons is 127 points better than the second-place Ravens, 290 points better than the third-place Chiefs and 490 points better than the fifth-place Packers. Despite clearly being the best regular-season team in the NFL during Allen's tenure, the Bills have made zero Super Bowls and just two AFC Championship Games.

The 2025 Bills led the league in rushing yards per game, finishing second in rushing yards per play, while the offense also finished fourth in yards per pass play. The Bills offense also ranked top four in efficiency on third down, red zone and goal to go situations while leading the league in time of possession. The Achilles heel of the team came on defense, where they ranked 30th in yards allowed per rush, negating a strong pass defense. The Bills still managed to finish fifth in point differential on the season behind the Seahawks, Rams, Patriots and Jaguars before winning a tight wild-card game in Jacksonville then losing an equally close divisional round game in Denver.
At the end of last season, Bills management and ownership cut ties with Sean McDermott, the head coach hired in 2017 who in his first season brought the Bills to the playoffs for the first time in 18 years. For nearly two decades, getting to the playoffs was a pipe dream in Buffalo. With a perennial MVP candidate at quarterback, getting to the playoffs has ceased to be good enough. Joe Brady moves from offensive coordinator to head coach with the hope he can be the one to crack the Super Bowl enigma in Orchard Park.
Despite the strong overall offensive numbers, the Bills lacked a go-to receiving option last year, and they spent a key 2026 draft pick to acquire one in D.J. Moore. Otherwise, the priority was on overhauling the defense to better fit new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's vision for the unit, parting ways with former key defenders such as Matt Milano, Taron Johnson, Tre'Davious White and Jordan Poyer. One thing that hasn't changed is GM Brandon Beane trying to catch lightning in a bottle with aging prominent edge rushers, with Bradley Chubb as the new Joey Bosa/Von Miller.

But if you do believe Brady has what it takes to improve upon the foundation McDermott built, I see value in the Coach of the Year market, where Brady has much longer odds than Jesse Minter (+1000) in a similar situation.

title: Preseason rankings on “The Athletic.” Where do the Cardinals sit?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are full-bore into training camp. This new offense is getting all the press, and most players are getting it, yet there is still a ton of work left to do. Did someone say “hope the offensive line improves?” Last month, ESPN published its Top-10 NFL players at every position, and few Cardinals […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - JULY 26: Mike LaFleur (R) of the Arizona Cardinals talks with defensive coordinator Nick Rallis during a team practice ahead of the NFL season at State Farm Stadium on July 26, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are full-bore into training camp. This new offense is getting all the press, and most players are getting it, yet there is still a ton of work left to do. Did someone say “hope the offensive line improves?” Last month, ESPN published its Top-10 NFL players at every position, and few Cardinals made the lists. RELATED: ESPN RANKS CARDINALS OFFENSIVE WEAPONS #6 As the preseason games are on the horizon, The Athletic has come out with its 2026 NFL rankings compiled by Josh Kendall. Where do the Cardinals rank? What about the remainder of the NFC West Division? Kendall states: “Training camps are open across the NFL, and the Hall of Fame Game kicks off next week, so we’re checking in on what’s new for all 32 teams and looking at how they stack up heading into the 2026 season.” —————————————————————————— #1 Los Angeles Rams A pretty much “well duh” observation before the season begins. The Rams were already a really good football team and was a single game away from getting back to the Super Bowl. When they traded for EDGE rusher Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns, that sealed their standing. It is still wide open if DT Aaron Donald will un-retire. Kendall’s assessment: “And maybe Aaron Donald? The Rams traded for the best defensive end in the league, and there has been summer scuttlebutt that they could coax one of the best defensive tackles of the last 20 years out of retirement. They also added two new — and pricey — cornerbacks. Unless this wide receiver corps collapses under the weight of age and extracurricular activities, Los Angeles has everything it needs for another Super Bowl run.” #5 Seattle Seahawks The Hawks have a great defense, and one of the league’s best receivers. They are a really good team. The Cardinals were losing to them by two touchdowns late in the fourth quarter last year, then tied the game up only to have Seattle walk down the field in just 28 seconds. What a heartbreaker. No telling what would have happened in overtime. The Seahawks ownership group mic dropped by selling the team. Kendall’s said this about the current league champion: “A group led by the family of Sun Microsystems co-founder Vinod Khosla just bought the reigning Super Bowl champions. All the other offseason news is about losses as running back Kenneth Walker, outside linebacker Boye Mafe and defensive backs Coby Bryant and Tariq Woolen are all gone via free agency. A repeat is not going to be easy.” #7 San Francisco 49ers Well, we knew the Niners would be right in the mix somewhere. That ranking is actually in the Top-10. Impressive for the division. Kendall’s said this: “Jauan Jennings and Kendrick Bourne are gone, and Brandon Aiyuk is in (maybe permanent?) limbo. But Mike Evans, Christian Kirk and surprise second-round draft pick De’Zhaun Stribling are Niners now. As long as star running back Christian McCaffrey stays healthy, the receivers won’t be the focal point of the offense anyway. But it’s worth noting McCaffrey tallied a career-high 413 regular-season touches last year, along with 37 more in the playoffs.” #30 Arizona Cardinals When the Las Vegas Raiders, New York Football Giants, Cleveland Browns, and Tennessee Titans outrank your team, you know things just ain’t right. Kendall is not giving this new Cardinals offense a single looksy. Part of the reason is that the QB position remains in flux, and the defense still needs a pass rusher. Kendall gave this reason for shoving the Cardinals to the basement without any supper: “Arizona and Murray tried to make it work. The No. 1 pick in the 2019 draft spent seven years wandering the desert, while the Cardinals managed to put together one winning season and no playoff wins. Now it’s Jacoby Brissett and what should be a full commitment to a rebuild under new head coach Mike LaFleur.” ———————————————————————————- That’s it? Three sentences? And two were about a player that is no longer on the roster? Nothing about the selection of the best running back in the draft. No verbiage regarding three of five offensive linemen have been replaced. Where is the part about Trey McBride’s most likely status as the best tight end in the league? What about the coming-out party for receiver Michael Wilson, and if Marv Harrison can have a great season, will provide this offense with fireworks? Everyone gets that Arizona has a new head coach. It is understood that a new offense is being installed and may take a while to get. We understand that the most likely candidate for the starting quarterback is either a career backup, a journeyman, or a rookie third-rounder. And yes, the Cardinals’ best pass rusher either is or is not happy where he is. With these rankings, which are one person’s professional opinion, the low point on the totem pole means there is just one direction this team can go this season.
