title: Falcons lock up G Matthew Bergeron to 4-year deal
summary: While we wait for Bijan Robinson to get his mega deal, the Atlanta Falcons are still busy locking up their own. The latest contract is for Matthew Bergeron, who was heading into the final year of his rookie deal. Bergeron, selected 38th in 2023, was clearly held in high regard by the incoming coaching staff […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 28: Matthew Bergeron #65 of the Atlanta Falcons is introduced prior to the NFL 2025 game between Washington Commanders and Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Atlanta, United States. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images While we wait for Bijan Robinson to get his mega deal, the Atlanta Falcons are still busy locking up their own. The latest contract is for Matthew Bergeron, who was heading into the final year of his rookie deal. Bergeron, selected 38th in 2023, was clearly held in high regard by the incoming coaching staff and new offensive line coach Bill Callahan. The 26-year-old has been the starter at left guard continuously since his rookie season in 2023, starting and appearing in 49 of 51 possible games while grading out as an above average starter in 2024 and 2025. Last year, Bergeron was only blamed for one sack, per Pro Football Focus, and his 28 total pressures allowed were far less than Chris Lindstrom, Jake Matthews, and (obviously) Elijah Wilkinson gave up. His run blocking grade, meanwhile, was third on the team behind Lindstrom and Ryan Neuzil and 16th among NFL guards with at least 200 snaps. Bergeron is both experienced enough and durable enough for the team to feel good about relying on and young enough to still reach greater heights, even if he has yet to be an elite player for longer than a few games at a time. The #Falcons and G Matthew Bergeron have agreed to terms on a four-year, $96 million contract extension, sources tell me and @JFowlerESPN . The 38th overall pick in 2023 gets $60 million guaranteed in a deal done by @Chase_Callahan of @excelfootball . pic.twitter.com/HwbDfp3sVJ — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 1, 2026 Fellow starting guard Chris Lindstrom got a 5 year, $105 million deal with $62.7 million guaranteed back in 2023, so Bergeron’s hefty raise is a reflection of rising valuations and cap space since then. It’s likely to strike more than a few Falcons fans as an overpay, but the Falcons very clearly viewed Bergeron’s signing as a major priority. Per Tori McElhaney at AtlantaFalcons.com : “Matthew is the type of player you build around,” Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham said. “He’s establishing himself as one of the top young guards in the NFL, and his toughness, consistency and leadership have made him a cornerstone of our offensive line and the culture we’re building in Atlanta.” That’s a strong endorsement, and clear proof that Kevin Stefanski and Bill Callahan wanted him to be a key piece of the offensive line. With uncertainty at right tackle and Jake Matthews aging at left tackle, the Falcons at least have stability and genuine talent at guard for the next few seasons. Now the next move is getting a deal done with Bijan, the man Bergeron is here to pave the way for. The Falcons will have a lot of money tied up into a handful of key offensive linemen and position players when the summer is over, and all of these players will need to be great in 2026 for an offense with question marks at quarterback to excel. That’s clearly both the hope and the plan for Atlanta. Congratulations to Bergeron, and may he and the Falcons offense reach new heights in 2026.

summary: The Falcons welcomed all fans for the first time on Saturday for the fourth consecutive day of training camp. Practice wasn’t quite as exciting as I hoped, but […]
full_text: FLOWERY BRANCH, GEORGIA - JULY 29: Kyle Pitts Sr. #8 reacts with Drake London #5 of the Atlanta Falcons during training camp at IBM Performance Field on July 29, 2026 in Flowery Branch, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons welcomed all fans for the first time on Saturday for the fourth consecutive day of training camp. It was a mercifully cool, cloud-covered morning, and fans turned out starting early. The line was already growing when I arrived at the facility before 8:00 am. Practice wasn’t quite as exciting as I hoped, but we continue to learn more and more about the construction of this roster and who will be competing for the few open starting jobs. Pretty good crowd here on Saturday as we're about to get underway pic.twitter.com/pzVJkxo802 — Kevin Knight (@FalcoholicKevin) August 1, 2026 Here are my notes from Day 4 of Falcons training camp. A relatively short practice, just over an hour. Both practices I’ve been to so far have been shorter than I’m used to. This was also not as high-energy as Friday. All four QBs participated to some extent. Tua was still very limited and didn’t participate in any team drills today. Michael Penix participated in everything except 11-on-11. Of the QBs, Cooper Rush had the strongest day. He looks more in control and is getting more comfortable. Michael Penix had a better day accuracy-wise but was let down by a number of drops. Jack Strand continued his up-and-down play, but still looks better than expected for a UDFA playing with starters. Overall, today was dominated by the defense. The coverage continued to be smothering and the pass rush notched multiple sacks. The Falcons continued to play a mix of fronts, including 3-4 and 4-2-5 packages. There was a lot of rotation up front with Brandon Dorlus, Da’Shawn Hand, Maason Smith, LaCale London, and Chris Williams all getting opportunities. At EDGE the initial grouping of Jalon Walker and Samson Ebukam continued, but we also saw Azeez Ojulari get involved with a sack. Bralen Trice and Cameron Thomas both came in for a base package look. James Pearce Jr. continues to work his way back, playing mostly with the depth groups. The linebacker situation was more fluid today. Christian Harris got the initial reps next to Divine Deablo, but the team rotated in Harold Perkins Jr. and Kendal Daniels at various times. Speaking of Rookie LB Kendal Daniels, he was back at practice after a schedule rest day on Friday. Daniels was impressive, with some nice coverage on Austin Hooper in teams. Veteran Darnay Holmes got the initial start in the slot today, but A.J. Woods and Sydney Brown also rotated in. Rookie Avieon Terrell had a mix of slot and outside snaps working mostly with the depth groups. Jahan Dotson’s role continues to grow, as he looked pretty clearly like the WR2 today. He got open quickly in team drills and caught several passes. Zachariah Branch nearly had a TD catch after getting open over the middle but didn’t quite get his head around in time. Of the rest of the receivers, Chris Blair has been the most consistently impressive. New punter Jake Bailey was crushing it today, with some really impressive punts. Atlanta is rotating in a lot of players at the gunner spots to try and find the best fit. There’s a lot of movement at multiple spots on offense and defense. The team is giving a lot of players opportunities to mix in. It sounds like the competition for the open starting spots will extend throughout the month. Michael Penix to Jahan Dotson #Falcons pic.twitter.com/4qVXgPtHhc — Kevin Knight (@FalcoholicKevin) August 1, 2026 Tech permitting (fingers crossed) we’ll try to have a live show for you all later today, so stay tuned for that. In the meantime, there’s no practice on Sunday as the team has their first off day. We’ll be back at practice bright and early on Monday for the first day in pads!

title: Ravens’ pass rush dominates 3rd day of training camp
summary: Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver was all smiles after Friday’s training camp practice. He had reason to be. His defense had just closed practice with four straight red zone stops. Second-year safety Malaki Starks capped off the final stand with an interception that forced the offense to do push-ups before heading into The Castle. […]
full_text: OWINGS MILLS, MARYLAND - JULY 29: Trey Hendrickson #91 of the Baltimore Ravens participates in a drill on the first day of training camp at Under Armour Performance Center Baltimore Ravens on July 29, 2026 in Owings Mills, Maryland. (Photo by Jamie Sabau/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver was all smiles after Friday’s training camp practice. He had reason to be. His defense had just closed practice with four straight red zone stops. Second-year safety Malaki Starks capped off the final stand with an interception that forced the offense to do push-ups before heading into The Castle. On that play and several others, the Ravens’ pass rushers made an impact, consistently forcing the quarterbacks to throw off-platform or out of rhythm. Trey Hendrickson, who struggled against left tackle Ronnie Stanley during his time as a Bengal, has gotten the better of his new teammate a number of times to open camp. Mike Green has given right tackle Roger Rosengarten fits, and Tavius Robinson has wreaked havoc from multiple spots along the defensive line. Undrafted rookie Ethan Burke has also flashed. On Friday, he combined with UDFA defensive tackle Aaron Graves for back-to-back pressures, including a well-executed stunt/loop that sent Burke into the quarterback’s lap. The 6-foot-6, 257-pound Texas product is high-cut but a fluid mover with surprising bend. He could be a dark horse for the fifth spot in the edge rusher room. What’s more, Baltimore has been able to generate this consistent pressure without their top three interior rushers: Nnamdi Madubuike, Travis Jones, and Calais Campbell. Once all of his options are at his disposal, Weaver thinks his job as DC will be “pretty easy.” “You do not have to try to scheme up free runners or things like that,” he said. “You can use the complexity of illusion to let those guys go win.” Weaver could be hinting at the Ravens’ plan for their revamped pass rush. Streamlining edge rushers’ responsibilities and using more line games on the interior are both ways to get home with four while maintaining numbers in coverage. That would be appropriate synergy between a head coach with a secondary background and a defensive coordinator who has played and coached the defensive line position for more than two decades. title: Buffalo Bills injuries: S C.J. Gardner-Johnson suffers lower calf strain
summary: The Buffalo Bills received encouraging news late on Saturday, August 1, with further tests revealing that safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson suffered only “a lower calf strain.” ESPN senior NFL insider Adam Schefter, citing anonymous sources, was first to share the injury update on Gardner-Johnson. Initial reports out of St. John Fisher University Saturday morning showed considerable […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 28: C.J. Gardner-Johnson #35 of the Chicago Bears warms up prior to an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills received encouraging news late on Saturday, August 1, with further tests revealing that safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson suffered only “ a lower calf strain .” ESPN senior NFL insider Adam Schefter, citing anonymous sources, was first to share the injury update on Gardner-Johnson. Initial reports out of St. John Fisher University Saturday morning showed considerable concern, with several people calling attention the fact that the team’s athletic trainers were looking closely at Gardner-Johnson’s lower rear leg . When Gardner-Johnson was helped off the field and went to the medical tent only to then be seen hitching a cart ride to the locker room, murmurs of the word “Achilles” began to surface. It would turn out to be an honest bit of overreaction by many outside observers, with any season-ending fears all but put to bed by left tackle Dion Dawkins when speaking with reporters after practice. Prior to the latest report of a strained calf, Dawkins informed those gathered around him that he walked up to Gardner-Johnson asking: “‘You alright? Take care of yourself — can you walk?’ And he got up and he did his thing, he could put weight on his legs, so he can walk,” adding “he’s alright.” Dawkins’ comments are stone-cold reminder that injuries thrive in the violence of NFL football. It’s warranted to have shown so much concern for Gardner-Johnson’s health, especially when there’s a chance that any number of other serious outcomes could have been diagnosed. We don’t know the severity of the injury, but multiple medical outlets debrief that a Grade 1 strain to the area takes anywhere between one to three weeks to heal. A Grade 2 lower calf strain can take anywhere from four to eight weeks to fully heal. Thankfully, this appears to be a minor setback for one of the Bills’ biggest personalities, and someone who could play a serious role during the 2026 NFL season.

title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting report: OT Spencer Brown
summary: The Buffalo Bills have worked tirelessly to build a strong offensive line. Protecting the franchise quarterback is essential, and president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane has done well to surround Josh Allen with an excellent group of protectors. However, that offensive line group is also opening holes for people like NFL rushing leader James […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 17: Spencer Brown #79 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates a touchdown scored by Keon Coleman against the Denver Broncos during the third quarter in the AFC Divisional Playoff game at Empower Field At Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills have worked tirelessly to build a strong offensive line. Protecting the franchise quarterback is essential, and president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane has done well to surround Josh Allen with an excellent group of protectors. However, that offensive line group is also opening holes for people like NFL rushing leader James Cook III. Whether via the draft or free agency, Beane has not been shy about ensuring that Buffalo has plenty of depth up front. Perhaps ironically, the Bills don’t have any projected starters on the offensive line who were first-round draft picks, but that same factoid also shows how well Beane and the team’s scouting staff has identified quality players on the offensive line. In today’s edition of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss a former third-round pick of the Bills who has developed into an elite presence at right tackle. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Spencer Brown Number: 79 Position: RT Height/Weight: 6’8”, 311 pounds Age: 28 (29 on 2/28/2027) Experience/Draft: 6; selected by Buffalo in the third round (No. 93 overall) of the 2021 NFL Draft College: Northern Iowa Acquired: Third-round draft choice Financial situation (per Spotrac): Brown enters the second year of the four year, $72 million extension he signed prior to last season. His cap hit for the 2026 season is $8.181 million. If he’s released, Buffalo would carry a dead cap charge in excess of $32 million, which they would split between this season ($9,677,000) and next season ($22,580,000). 2025 Recap: Brown started at right tackle for the Bills once again last season, and he brought the nasty to the offensive line as he has for his entire career. He continued to show out as one of the best run blockers at right tackle in the NFL, earning a top-ten run block grade from Pro Football Focus . The analytics site graded him at an 85.3 in that phase of the game, which was seventh among 89 qualifying offensive tackles. PFF wasn’t as rosy on Brown as a pass blocker, grading him at a 61.3, which was 66th among 89 qualifying offensive tackles. Overall, his grade was a 76.6, which was 20th at his position. Brown was called for just four penalties , a huge improvement from the 15 flags he drew during the 2025 season. He missed three games last year, sitting in Week Four against the New Orleans Saints thanks to a calf issue before he missed games against the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals later in the season thanks to a shoulder injury. He returned to play in time for the playoffs, though, and started both of Buffalo’s playoff contests. Positional outlook: Brown is one of six players listed at offensive tackle on the current roster. Dion Dawkins and Chase Lundt are listed only at tackle. Jude Bowry and Tylan Grable are listed at tackle and guard. Travis Clayton is listed as an offensive tackle, but he played some defensive tackle during offseason workouts. 2026 Offseason: Brown says he will be ready for the first day of training camp, but he missed time this offseason while he recouperated from his various injuries last season. He had a minor knee surgery this offseason, as well. 2026 Season outlook: Barring something strange, Brown will be the starting right tackle once again this season. He earned every bit of that huge extension, and while injuries prevented him from playing in all 17 games last season, there’s no question that Buffalo’s offensive line is better when he’s available. Availability has really been the only question mark with Brown during his career. Only once—in 2023—did Brown play every game. However, Brown has never played fewer than 13 games in a season, either. With a newcomer entering the line at left guard, it will be nice to see the right side continue to work as a unit, as Brown and right guard O’Cyrus Torrence will work together yet again. In terms of expected points added (EPA), the right side of Buffalo’s offensive line was tied for the eleventh-best combination in the league last year, as runs to that direction resulted in .07 EPA per play. Buffalo has a lot of beef on that right side, and Brown combines mountainous size with superb athleticism, which allows him to do plenty of damage at multiple levels of the defense while clearing room for a potent rushing attack. In short, there isn’t any drama here. If Brown is healthy, he is the starter at right tackle. If he is the starter at right tackle, then the Bills are in good hands.

full_text: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #42: S Colin Jones Well this one just so happens to coincide with the jersey number, as we celebrate former safety/cornerback and special teams player, The Ace That Runs The Place COLIN JONES! Jones was drafted in the 6th round of the 2011 NFL Draft by the San Francisco 49ers, and spent one season there before the Panthers acquired him in August of 2012, shipping off a 2014 7th round pick for his services. This transaction turned out to be a bargain, as Colin Jones played in 124 games as a Panther from 2012 to 2019 in various capacities, mostly as a special teams ace, but he did start 14 games as either a spot starter at safety, and even as a nickel cornerback at times in a pinch. Jones logged 3 interceptions and 7 pass deflections when called upon in these duties, but he will always be remembered as a special teams player, and a stalwart one for this team. I know, I know, there’s likely going to be booing in the comment section. But, I have prepared my arguments for why Colin Jones belongs on this list. First of all, in the two seasons Colin Jones started 3 or more games (2015-3 starts, 2017-7 starts), the Panthers made the playoffs! Secondly, Colin Jones is the second most veteran DEFENSIVE BACK in Carolina Panthers history with 124 games played for the franchise, trailing only Mike Minter with 148 games played. He is the 7th most veteran defender in general for the Panthers, trailing only Thomas Davis, Julius Peppers, Mike Minter, Charles Johnson, Mike Rucker, and Jason Kyle in games played for the franchise. The Ace That Runs The Place is low-key one of the better trades the Panthers have ever made, trading away a 7th round pick two years out from the transaction. What they got was a special teams ace who stepped in to whatever role was needed when called upon, and spent 7 seasons in Carolina doing so. While fans often wanted to see him released during that time for the shiny, new undrafted free agents to serve as safety 4/5 on the depth chart, I truly hope the heart has grown fonder now that we can look back half a decade later at his services. And we’ll always have this crazy interception , and his run on a fake punt . When all was said and done, Jones very much embodied the Keep Pounding philosophy in the sense of simply doing the job he was asked of, even if it was doing something like playing nickel corner since the Panthers didn’t value depth corners during the large portion of his career. Maybe that’s on the coaches, or maybe they had the knowledge that the answer was on the roster already. Either way, celebrate the Ace down below!

summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. full_text: HOUSTON, TX - FEBRUARY 1: Running back DeShaun Foster #20 of the Carolina Panthers scores on a 33 yard touchdown run against the New England Patriots during Super Bowl XXXVIII at Reliant Stadium on February 1, 2004 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Brian Bahr/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #43. DeShaun Foster On Friday, running back Stephen Davis was our player of honor in the countdown of top 100 Panthers. One day later, it’s his former partner in crime, DeShaun Foster. Serendipity. People forget that DeShaun Foster was actually born in Charlotte, coincidentally enough, but he grew up in California and went to college at UCLA. After a standout career there, the Panthers brought him home by making him the 32nd overall pick in the 2002 NFL Draft. Unfortunately, his rookie season ended before it even got started, as a preseason injury took him out for the season. He returned to back up Stephen Davis for his second year, and while his contributions over the course of the season were modest, he was responsible for two of the most memorable plays in Panthers history during their playoff run. First, he broke free from six different Eagles defenders for a two yard touchdown in the NFC Championship game. Then, in the Super Bowl, he broke free for a 35 yard touchdown run that ended with an iconic dive over the goal line that spurred a comeback in a truly unhinged fourth quarter. The injury issues that popped up upon Foster’s entry to the league returned to plague him for much of the rest of his career. He missed the majority of his third season with a broken collarbone. He made it through his fourth season largely in good health, and even supplanted Stephen Davis as the team’s starter by season’s end, but he broke his ankle in the playoffs. His effectiveness began to wane after that, and he gradually ceded more of his workload to the newly drafted DeAngelo Williams over his final two seasons in Carolina. He got a cup of coffee in San Francisco to wrap up his career. When all was said and done, Foster amassed 3,336 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns across five seasons in Carolina. He never topped 1,000 yards in a season, but he amassed just under 900 yards in each of his last three seasons as a Panther, and he chipped in here and there as a receiver out of the backfield. The 3,336 yards are good for sixth in Panthers history. Between the stat compilation and the iconic moments in the playoffs, Foster earns himself spot number 43 on the top 100 Panthers of all time.

title: Bears Veterans Are Seeing a Different Team Take Shape
summary: The Chicago Bears held multiple player press conferences following Day 4 of training camp on Saturday, including pressers with tight end Cole Kmet and cornerback Jaylon Johnson. Both were selected by Chicago in the 2020 NFL Draft, making them the longest-tenured players on the roster. Now entering their seventh season with the organization, Kmet and […]
full_text: The Chicago Bears held multiple player press conferences following Day 4 of training camp on Saturday, including pressers with tight end Cole Kmet and cornerback Jaylon Johnson. Both were selected by Chicago in the 2020 NFL Draft, making them the longest-tenured players on the roster. Now entering their seventh season with the organization, Kmet and Johnson have experienced many transformations the Bears have undergone over the past six years. From various coaching staffs and quarterbacks to major roster changes, their perspective offers a unique look at how the team has evolved and why this year’s group feels different. Both players spoke about those changes during their press conferences. “It’s a different feel to camp than maybe in years past,” Kmet said. “I’ve spent a lot of my career wondering what’s next and how’s tomorrow going to go. I feel like I kinda know what to expect at this point, especially with this staff, and what they want to get done and what they expect from each individual.” Kmet pointed to the continuity within the current coaching staff and the clarity of expectations as a major difference compared to previous training camps. “It’s nice coming in and getting ready for a season understanding how you fit in the scheme of things, and then also the direction of this offense, where we want it go, and the identity we want to forge.” He described the start of this year’s training camp as “operationally sound.” Johnson echoed similar sentiments, noting that the changes within the team have translated to the field and are reflected in the confidence and talent he has seen from this year’s group during training camp. “This is the best offense I’ve had in 7 years, as far as going against them … Caleb’s the best quarterback I’ve had since maybe Nick Foles if you want to go back that far. Just as far as slinging it, he’s doing his thing. You can see the accuracy. You can see the confidence throwing the ball in tight windows.” He also highlighted the players’ buy-in to the offensive system and the belief the unit has in itself. Bears CB Jaylon Johnson has high expectations for Caleb and the Bears offense 👀 🎥 via @ChicagoBears #NFLonDAZN #BearDown pic.twitter.com/YUm1kzAYOn — NFL on DAZN (@NFLonDAZN) August 1, 2026 Training camp is still in its early stages, and there is still plenty to prove before the Bears take the field for a regular-season game. However, for veterans like Kmet and Johnson, the changes within the team have created a sense that this is a different chapter in Chicago.

summary: This morning, the Chicago Bears canceled the “open” part of practice due to inclement weather, and fans were sent home. It was raining, and there was lightning in the area, so they began practice indoors at the Walter Payton Center. The decision wasn’t made until well after many fans had already gathered at Hawthorn Mall, […]
full_text: LAKE FOREST, IL - AUGUST 12: Chicago Bears fans line up to go through security to enter the Bears training session in action during a joint practice between the Chicago Bears and the Miami Dolphins on August 12, 2021 at Halas Hall in Lake Forest, IL. (Photo by Robin Alam/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images This morning, the Chicago Bears canceled the “open” part of practice due to inclement weather, and fans were sent home. It was raining, and there was lightning in the area, so they began practice indoors at the Walter Payton Center. The decision wasn’t made until well after many fans had already gathered at Hawthorn Mall, boarded buses to Lake Forest, unloaded, and lined up at the gates at Halas Hall. Today’s theme was Kids Day, and the Bears had plenty of kid-friendly activities, entertainment, and experiences planned around the facility. It’s unfortunate, especially for fans who traveled a long way, but the Walter Payton Center isn’t equipped to accommodate fans. Weather-related issues have seemingly arisen every year the Bears have held training camp at Halas Hall due to the limited availability of the free tickets. It’s also why attendance numbers are nowhere near what they were when camp was at Olivet Nazarene University in Bourbonnais, Illinois. Back then, there was no cap on the number of free tickets you could get for camp, but Halas Hall has a much smaller footprint than a college. Fans want to go, but they just can’t. Fans were pissed about being sent away today, and some turned to social media to express that, but what are the Bears supposed to do? They can’t just let in a few dozen to watch from the viewing area above the indoor field. They aren’t going to have fans wandering around the practice fields in the rain with nothing going on. The Bears did give fans who couldn’t make it today a 15% discout on merchandise, so there’s that. Yay. My two tips for traveling to Bears camp. One: have a backup plan, because weather-related issues will happen. There are plenty of other things to do in the Chicagoland area, so make a day out of the trip. Two: never buy the free tickets from the scalping scum who scoop them up to make a quick buck because they aren’t giving refunds on free. I was fortunate to get tickets for the first several years the camp was at Halas Hall, but the last two years, I was completely shut out by Ticketmaster. It’s an awful system for getting tickets, and I hope the Bears are having internal discussions on how to improve it. The Bears are off tomorrow, Monday’s practice is a private community day, and then they have three open practices in a row. The pads will be on, so we’ll learn more about the trenches next week. The Bears’ offense had the edge the first week of training camp, so if you’re buying the hype, our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook have Caleb Williams with the ninth-best odds for league MVP at +1500.

title: Cash, Stash, or Slash: Garrett Bradbury
summary: As we continue to look at the future of the Chicago Bears and what should be done contract-wise with some key veteran players who don’t have many years left on their contracts, today we pivot back to the offensive line and look at Garrett Bradbury. Drew Dalman certainly threw the Bears a curveball when he […]
full_text: LAKE FOREST, ILLINOIS - JUNE 3: Garrett Bradbury #67 of the Chicago Bears stretches during a Chicago Bears OTA Offseason Workout at Halas Hall on June 3, 2026 in Lake Forest, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we continue to look at the future of the Chicago Bears and what should be done contract-wise with some key veteran players who don’t have many years left on their contracts, today we pivot back to the offensive line and look at Garrett Bradbury. Drew Dalman certainly threw the Bears a curveball when he retired in the spring. The Bears, not knowing how the draft would play out, needed to find a center they could trust and find one quickly, and they did just that, acquiring Garrett Bradbury from the New England Patriots. Six weeks later, they were able to add Logan Jones in the 2nd round of the NFL Draft, and it’s that selection that cements Bradbury’s future with the team. Garrett Bradbury: Slash If some of the Bears’ top targets at center had gone off the board before them and the Bears selected a day three center with less certainty, I think this probably would have been a “stash” situation and see how Bradbury and the rookie play this year and make decisions in January. However, Logan Jones was the Bears’ top choice at center,r and he was the first center taken off the board in the NFL Draft. Jones is an experienced college player who has already had every accolade heaped upon him that you could imagine. It’s hard to look at Jones and not think he can at least be a functional center at the NFL level. We don’t know how good Jones is going to be, but he’s going to have to fail before the Bears consider anyone else, and I don’t think fans, media, or the Bears expect him to fail. With Jones in tow, Bradbury is locked into being a one-year player with the Bears. The Bears will almost certainly let Bradbury walk after his contract expires and fully pivot to Jones in 2027. The only question really is: will Jones or Bradbury be the starting center for the bulk of the games in the 2026 season? That certainly will play out in training camp, and we will have to see how the coaches see that one going. Bradbury was a move the Bears had to make. They had uncertainty at a position that is critical for Ben Johnson’s offense. They need a smart, reliable center who can make calls and put the offense in a position to succeed. They had that with Dalman. Bradbury can do that role decently until Jones is ready to take over. Whether Jones is ready in August, November, or 2027, we know it’s coming; it’s just a matter of when.

title: The time is now for DJ Ivey to prove he belongs
summary: After overcoming a devastating knee injury, Cincinnati Bengals cornerback DJ Ivey enters the biggest season of his NFL career with an opportunity to earn a permanent role in the secondary. DJ Ivey Cap Status Ivey is entering the final season of his four-year rookie contract after the Bengals selected him in the seventh round (246th overall) of […]
full_text: After overcoming a devastating knee injury, Cincinnati Bengals cornerback DJ Ivey enters the biggest season of his NFL career with an opportunity to earn a permanent role in the secondary. DJ Ivey Height: 6-foot-1 Weight: 192 pounds Age: 26 College: Miami (FL) Hometown: Homestead, Florida Experience: 3 years Cap Status Ivey is entering the final season of his four-year rookie contract after the Bengals selected him in the seventh round (246th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft. He is scheduled to earn a base salary of $1.145 million while carrying a cap hit of approximately $1.17 million. He will become an unrestricted free agent following the 2026 season. Background Seventh-round draft picks rarely enjoy long NFL careers. Many never make a 53-man roster. Ivey has already beaten those odds. A five-year starter at Miami, Ivey entered the NFL with the size, length, and athleticism teams covet in an outside cornerback. The Bengals believed he was worth developing, and he rewarded that faith by making the roster as a rookie. Unfortunately, just as his role began to expand during the 2023 season, Ivey suffered a torn ACL that ended his rookie campaign and forced him to spend much of the following year working his way back to full strength. Rather than allowing the injury to define him, though, Ivey quietly continued developing. He appeared in every game during the 2025 season, providing valuable depth in the secondary while becoming an important contributor on special teams. Although he played only limited defensive snaps, he finished the year with 12 tackles and three passes defended, showing encouraging progress whenever his number was called. Outlook on the 2026 Season and Beyond Cornerback may be one of the deepest positions on Cincinnati’s roster, but that doesn’t mean opportunities won’t come. In today’s NFL, injuries are inevitable, and teams often rely on four, five, or even six cornerbacks over the course of a season. When an opportunity arrives, the Bengals need someone they can count on. That is where Ivey comes in. While he has already proven he can overcome adversity, now he must prove he can become more than just quality depth. The Bengals have invested heavily in rebuilding their defense, and competition throughout the secondary will be fierce. If Ivey continues the steady development he has shown since returning from injury, he has every opportunity to carve out a meaningful defensive role while remaining one of the club’s most valuable special teams players. But with guys like Ceyair Wright, Bralyn Lux, and Ja’Sir Taylor also vying for roster spots, Ivey needs a good showing in camp and the preseason just to ensure he keeps his spot on the Bengals’ 53-man roster.

He has been a dominant force, and not all of that has been because of his physical ability. The game is just as much mental—even down in the trenches—in the NFL. This is an example of why Cincinnati felt comfortable giving up that pick in the draft. Lawrence has been getting involved with teammates since the team brought him in. full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JULY 29: Chase Brown #30 of the Cincinnati Bengals performs during the Cincinnati Bengals Training Camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields on July 29, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images A downpour moved the start of Day 4 of Bengals training camp into their indoor practice facility, but they eventually moved back outside to the Kettering Health Practice Fields. Saturday was the final of a four-day stretch to start camp, with an off day tomorrow and the first day of pads on Monday. Here are some of the best Twitter reactions from the great members of the local media who cover the Bengals. Just a bunch of good, really competitive reps today. Offense wins some. Defense wins some. Good energy. Attention to detail and execution — Charlie Goldsmith (@CharlieG__) August 1, 2026 This is really good to hear. If Charlie Goldsmith is saying this, take note. Charlie is on top of every facet of the Bengals, so what he’s saying carries a lot of weight. Look, iron sharpens iron. That was the hope for the Bengals going into camp, and it appears as if that is exactly what’s happening. If it’s evenly matched between the offense and defense throughout camp, that’s the best-case scenario. Andrei Iosivas catches the pass from Joe Burrow in stride #Bengals @WCPO pic.twitter.com/rEYmQIfd3a — Noelle Blumel (@NoelleBlumel) August 1, 2026 First off, Noelle is crushing it on the Bengals beat. She’s only been working at WCPO for a few months, but you can already tell her passion for sports and working in sports media. Give her a follow on Twitter. If the Bengals can hit plays like this in the regular season, good luck to any opposing defense trying to stop this offense. This is an absolute rainbow throw by Joe Burrow, and a terrific catch in stride by Andrei Iosivas. Every great wide receiver duo throughout NFL history has had that WR3 as their third wheel, and Iosivas can still be that for the Bengals. First big defensive play of 11 on 11 belongs to DJ Turner. Pass break up on the throw to Ja'Marr. #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/eRotlOU7n7 — Gabi Sorrentino (@GSorrentinoTV) August 1, 2026 Turner really had to work to get his hands on the football and break it up from Chase, which he did. Those two have been going at it throughout Training Camp, most notably in the scuffle that broke out on Day 1. Ja’Marr coming at ya pic.twitter.com/N3gHDmmnlj — Jay Morrison (@ByJayMorrison) August 1, 2026 This is Ja’Marr Chase at his best. Great route, great job getting the feet down, great ball control. You can’t defend this when Burrow and Chase are connecting like this. “This is about as grown man of a team as I’ve ever been a part of.” A must-listen to interview from #Bengals center Ted Karras pic.twitter.com/iNomYt1roO — Kelsey Conway (@KelseyLConway) August 1, 2026 Grown man. Even with all of the attention focusing on the defense in camp, the offensive line still matters. The fact that Ted Karras, one of the leaders of the Bengals’ offensive line, is describing the offensive line like this offers high expectations. Ted Karras believes this will be the best run blocking offensive line he’s played with in his time with the Bengals in part because they are going up against the defense that is as much a “grown-man team I’ve been a part of. It’s exciting.” pic.twitter.com/SC5aiJe3g7 — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) August 1, 2026 So much of the Bengals’ rebuilding of their offensive line has been focused on protecting Joe Burrow. But along with that is their ability and success in the running game. When the Bengals can run the football, that makes it even tougher to defend this offense. Joe Burrow with the scramble in Red zone Mitch Tinsley with the full out extension for the score. Tinsley appeared to have the wind knocked out of him as he landed on the ball. Suffered a cut under his lower lip from chin strap as face mask hit turf. pic.twitter.com/jg1GLBnMd4 — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) August 1, 2026 Mitchell Tinsley has looked really good in camp. For what it’s worth, go back and watch the Bengals win in Baltimore on Thanksgiving last season. Tinsley was spectacular in that game. The Bengals may need him at various points this season, so it’s really encouraging to see him perform through the first four days of camp. “Boom!” -Dexter Lawrence after stuffing a run #Bengals @WCPO pic.twitter.com/Y9vNMlmSBp — Noelle Blumel (@NoelleBlumel) August 1, 2026 There is clearly a different energy about the Bengals’ defense in camp, and it’s largely due to Dexter Lawrence. You can’t put a cap on the value of him being here. That’s a high compliment to pay any player. “Better bring your f-ing shit when you’re going against Dexter Lawrence.” Ted Karras being tested daily against the stud DT. Karras compared it to going up against the 2016 Patriots in practice. pic.twitter.com/j2GMQscxmB — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) August 1, 2026 Ted Karras is keeping it real. Again, iron is sharpening iron. For the record, that 2016 Patriots’ defensive line included Chris Long, on a defense that led the NFL in scoring and finished eighth in yards allowed per game. The #Bengals first block of camp is complete (3 practices, one walk-through) Cincinnati’s first off day is tomorrow. Pads go on Monday pic.twitter.com/hFpw2mwohf — Kelsey Conway (@KelseyLConway) August 1, 2026 Yup, the tone has been set. Pads go on Monday. It’s going to start to get real.
author: Alex Frank

title: Ja’Marr Chase already sees shades of Tee Higgins in Noah Thomas
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have only been a few practices into training camp, but rookie wide receiver Noah Thomas is already generating buzz from the people who matter most. Thursday’s practice featured one of the biggest offensive highlights of camp when the 6-foot-5 undrafted rookie climbed the ladder on a contested catch against cornerback DJ Ivey. The […]
full_text: Nov 28, 2025; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets defensive back Rodney Shelley (6) and defensive back Omar Daniels (9) break up a pass against Georgia Bulldogs wide receiver Noah Thomas (5) during the second half at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Cincinnati Bengals have only been a few practices into training camp, but rookie wide receiver Noah Thomas is already generating buzz from the people who matter most . Thursday’s practice featured one of the biggest offensive highlights of camp when the 6-foot-5 undrafted rookie climbed the ladder on a contested catch against cornerback DJ Ivey. The play became even more impressive when Thomas wrestled the football away after it appeared headed for an interception, turning a potential takeaway into a highlight-reel reception. That catch caught the attention of none other than Ja’Marr Chase. Speaking after practice, Chase praised Thomas’ ability to win in contested situations and pointed to the value of having another big-bodied receiver capable of making plays above the rim. Chase noted that’s the type of skill set Cincinnati can use, especially when it comes to winning jump-ball opportunities. “That’s an explosive, and that’s what we need. That’s another Tee Higgins. We’ve got somebody else to go there and get a jump ball,” Chase told Bengals.com . “I don’t really get jump balls like that. Joe usually leads me out in front. But seeing it from the younger guys and seeing what kind of catches they can make, contested catches, that’s what we need.” Thomas wasn’t limited to one splash play, either. Earlier in practice, he hauled in a well-placed pass from veteran quarterback Joe Flacco on a shorter route, continuing what’s becoming an encouraging start to camp. The former Georgia and Texas A&M receiver faces an uphill climb as an undrafted rookie in a crowded Bengals receiver room. Chase, Tee Higgins, Andrei Iosivas, newcomer Colbie Young, and Charlie Jones are all battling for roster spots and playing time, making every practice rep meaningful. Still, it’s hard to ask for a better way to stand out than making contested catches that earn praise from one of the NFL’s premier receivers. It’s still early, and one practice won’t secure Thomas a roster spot. But if he continues flashing his size, ball skills, and ability to finish through contact, he’ll give the Bengals plenty to think about as preseason games approach.
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Dan Pitcher is feeling good about the Bengals offensive line
summary: Cincinnati Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher is very high on his offensive line heading into the 2026 football season. Speaking with Dan Hoard, Pitcher said this is the best he’s felt about the Bengals offensive line. “I sit here in front of you feeling as good about that as I ever felt. You’ve got five […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher takes questions from the press during the annual season kickoff media day event at Paycor Stadium in downtown Cincinnati on Monday, July 27, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Cincinnati Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher is very high on his offensive line heading into the 2026 football season. Speaking with Dan Hoard , Pitcher said this is the best he’s felt about the Bengals offensive line. “I sit here in front of you feeling as good about that as I ever felt. You’ve got five guys that played together for the bulk of last season, who played their best football as the season went on, and there are a lot of measures that demonstrate that they got better and better and better.” The Bengals return all five starters from an offensive line that played its best football during the last 7 weeks of the football season. According to PFF, the Bengals had a top-five pass-blocking grade during those final 7 weeks of the season, once Dalton Risner took over as the starting right guard. The addition of Dalton Risner helped stabilize the Bengals offensive line. He will be one of the five returning starters in 2026. pic.twitter.com/IM5w1Y8K1m — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) July 20, 2026 Chemistry on the offensive line is such an underrated aspect for an offense. It is refreshing that the Bengals will return five capable starters to begin the 2026 season. If this unit finishes in the top 10 this season, the Bengals could set several offensive records.

full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JULY 29: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns throws a pass during Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on July 29, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Day 4 of Cleveland Browns training camp took place on Saturday, August 1. Both quarterbacks competing to start spoke to the media before practice. Cleveland Browns Training Camp Report – Day 4 (8/1/26) 1. Watson & Sanders Speak: QB Deshaun Watson and QB Shedeur Sanders are competing for the starting job in training camp, and each of them spoke to the media before Saturday’s practice. Here is a snippet from Watson saying he’d be open to signing a contract extension to stay in Cleveland when his current contract expires. That would only happen if he wins the job and lights the world on fire this year. You can read more on Watson here . Deshaun Watson would be open to signing a new contract with the #Browns when the current one expires after this season. "My wife and I have a house on the East Side. We love Cleveland." pic.twitter.com/PKhx9VcMaw — Jeff Schudel (@jsproinsider) August 1, 2026 During Sanders’ interview, he talked about some of the differences he sees in himself in year two, as well as the comfort level he has with Todd Monken’s offense. Shedeur Sanders discusses the differences between Year 1 and Year 2, explaining how much more comfortable he feels in Todd Monken’s offense. The game is slowing down, and that confidence is showing in his command, timing, and overall play. #Browns pic.twitter.com/xTbdN6Ro3e — Lance Reisland (Coach Riz) (@LanceReisland) August 1, 2026 2. Injuries Can Shift Momentum: For the second straight day, OG Teven Jenkins missed practice, allowing KT Leveston to work with the starters. Granted, the coaching staff isn’t going to make a decision solely based on training camp injuries, but it can make players fall out of favor in a competition. If you recall, QB Kenny Pickett missed much of camp last year, essentially eliminating him from the Browns’ quarterback competition. 3. A Bit to Unpack Here: Yesterday, I put in a little note about TE Jack Stoll making some catches when it’s not what he’s known for. Well, this might be an example why. Early in practice, QB Deshaun Watson threw a short pass to Stoll that he should have caught. Instead, S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren helped knock it away, tip it in the air, and then S Christopher Edmonds came up with the pick six. Edmonds had two interceptions on the day. 🚨tip drill🚨 pic.twitter.com/3Ae7mWsdin — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 1, 2026 4. Red Zone Drills: Much of practice involved the first installation of red zone drills, which meant a lot of touchdown opportunities. Unfortunately for the quarterbacks, it also led to quite a few interceptions, which the defense loved. Because they are just 7-on-7 drills, though, some of the touchdowns are pretty rudimentary, like this connection between QB Shedeur Sanders and WR Jerry Jeudy : #Browns Shedeur Sanders to Jerry Jeudy for a TD in goal line 7 on 7 pic.twitter.com/bJCmJG2MVS — Fred Greetham (@FredGreetham9) August 1, 2026 What you don’t like seeing is how bad an interception can be in drills, like when QB Deshaun Watson threw it right to S Donovan McMillan after he was pretty much just standing there the whole time: Donovan McMillon with the pick off Deshaun Watson in the end zone #Browns : pic.twitter.com/GeEBmvsTLu — Ashley Bastock (@AshleyBastock42) August 1, 2026 I was said that Watson had a few designed rollout touchdowns in red zone drlls. 5. Graham Continues Strong Start: I always say that it’s tough to evaluate offensive and defensive lines in camp, especially if pads aren’t on. Nonetheless, the defensive line has been bringing the heat, with DT Mason Graham consistently getting into the backfield. MASON GRAHAM WRECKING HAVOC 🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/kuddAa9Wrj — ESPN Cleveland (@ESPNCleveland) August 1, 2026 6. Star of Camp: Through four practices, WR Denzel Boston has been the star of camp, looking like a home run pick for early in the second round and possibly the team’s No. 1 receiver. First Fight of Training Camp: What started off as some post-snap jostling between C Elgton Jenkins and DE Sam Kamara turned into a fight between DE Alex Wright and RG KT Leveston . As is often the case in camp, the rest of the players were able to diffuse the situation. A little scuffle broke out during today's #Browns training camp practice. pic.twitter.com/cVQKvI3SVK — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) August 1, 2026 8. Just Missed: The Browns threw five interceptions on the day. It should have been six, but in one of the last red zone drills, QB Shedeur Sanders ’ pass for WR Jerry Jeudy was dropped by S Grant Delpit . Browns defense winning this red zone drill. Grant Delpit with a play. pic.twitter.com/Q57QQYHetz — Scott Petrak ct (@ScottPetrak) August 1, 2026 8. Deep Interceptions: To end practice, the quarterbacks were throwing downfield passes to the right side, but both Watson and Sanders were victims of interceptions. Here is Sanders getting picked off by CB D’Angelo Ross when trying to get the ball to WR Jerry Jeudy . Some people noted that they feel if this was WR Denzel Boston as the target, that he would’ve come down with the ball. Sanders picked off by D’Angelo Ross going against Jeudy down the right sideline #Browns pic.twitter.com/AGnRjnd7U2 — Ashley Bastock (@AshleyBastock42) August 1, 2026 And then, QB Deshaun Watson tried getting the ball to WR Tylan Wallace , but it over overthrown and intercepted by S Christopher Edmonds . Christopher Edmonds ends practice picking off Deshaun Watson on a ball intended for Tylan Wallace #Browns : pic.twitter.com/I23EoBp9f7 — Ashley Bastock (@AshleyBastock42) August 1, 2026 9. Zac Weighs In: It’s always nice to get a pulse on which players look particularly sharp in training camp, and Zac Jackson of The Athletic gave this list of five players who have stood out thus far. The five most impressive players of the first week of Browns camp from where I sit (mostly stand, takes me awhile to get up) Verse Ward Boston Graham Judkins No real order. And no clear leader at QB IMO but Sanders had a better throwing week. — Zac Jackson (@AkronJackson) August 1, 2026 10. Brownies: TE Harold Fannin returned from his personal absence day. … LB Carson Schwesinger did not practice, but watched from the sideline. … WR Luke Floriea got some yards on an end around. … Other players missing practice were WR Jamari Thrash , DT Kalia Davis , and TE Joe Royer (personal). … QB Dillon Gabriel has been noted by media as being the most consistent QB, although he was picked off by LB Reid Carrico to end practice. … 11. Up Next: The Browns are off on Sunday. They will practice on Monday at 1:30 PM ET. It will be open to the public.

title: Cleveland Browns: No one is ready to close the door on Deshaun Watson
summary: The Cleveland Browns, and by extension their fans, are so close that they can reach out and almost touch it. Four-and-a-half years after the Browns made their confessed “big swing and miss” on quarterback Deshaun Watson, the end is almost here as Watson enters the final year of his five-year, fully guaranteed contract. All the […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JULY 30: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns looks on during the Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on July 30, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns, and by extension their fans, are so close that they can reach out and almost touch it. Four-and-a-half years after the Browns made their confessed “big swing and miss” on quarterback Deshaun Watson, the end is almost here as Watson enters the final year of his five-year, fully guaranteed contract. All the Browns have to do is let the 2026 season play out, and once the final whistle blows on January 10, pack up Watson’s locker and have the contents delivered to him while the team prepares for another offseason of quarterback hunting. It is all right there for the taking, something so simple that there is no way anyone could mess this up. Except, what if Watson plays well enough this fall that the Browns convince themselves he is worthy of another contract? General manager Andrew Berry did not exactly close the door on that scenario while meeting with the media at training camp this week. With the idea that Watson has no future with the Browns past this season, Berry was asked why not just play another quarterback ? “I wouldn’t rule anything out in terms of the whole quarterback-of-the-future discussion. Ultimately, we’re going to play the player who’s the most productive on the field. I think Deshaun is only 30. There’s no need to make any decisions about the future right now. We’ll let it play out and figure it out as we go.” Owner Jimmy Haslam had the opportunity to put this all to rest on Friday during his media session, but would not completely rule out the seemingly improbable idea of Watson being around past this season : “I think there are all kinds of possibilities out there — so, yes. But here again, we’ve got to get through practice. Somebody might have a great year, and they’re our quarterback forever, or neither of them might. I think it’s way, way, way early to be talking about who’s going to be our quarterback next year — we’ve got to figure out who’s going to start the first game.” Those are both decent enough answers from Berry and Haslam, as it makes sense not to alienate a player you may need this fall or tip your hand on your plans. But given everything he has gone through since arriving in town – the 11-game suspension from the NFL, shoulder surgery, two tears of his Achilles tendon, and one of the largest drop-offs in production in NFL history- there is no way that Watson would want to stay with the Browns one moment longer than is necessary. Right? Deshaun Watson would be open to signing a new contract with the #Browns when the current one expires after this season. "My wife and I have a house on the East Side. We love Cleveland." pic.twitter.com/PKhx9VcMaw — Jeff Schudel (@jsproinsider) August 1, 2026 Well … that’s not how Watson is currently approaching the situation, as he explained during his media session on Saturday: “When I first got here, there was a lot of stuff going on as the world knows. I don’t have any bad feelings toward Cleveland; I love Cleveland. Me and my wife have a house on the East Side; we were around all summer. I haven’t had a bad experience outside of some different times in the stadium. I don’t know why that narrative is out there that people think I don’t like Cleveland. If the opportunity shows up, we’ll see where it goes.” Admittedly, this is all premature as there is a lot of football to be played before the Browns have to decide on Watson’s future. But this is still the same franchise that has bungled every quarterback it has made since 1999, including: not building an offensive line for Tim Couch using first-round draft picks on Brady Quinn, Brandon Weeden and Johnny Manziel, mismanaging the final years of Baker Mayfield’s time with the team, feeling it needs to “bend the knee” to the family of a fifth-round draft pick with a questionable future . So until they prove otherwise, it may be best to hold off on sending any goodbye cards to a certain veteran quarterback.
author: Thomas Moore

title: Todd Monken updates Browns QB competition, timing on making a decision
summary: At least according to our poll, Cleveland Browns fans feel confident that either they know who the starting quarterback should be already or will after the joint practice and preseason game with the Buffalo Bills: According to GM Andrew Berry (and as previously said by HC Todd Monken), the decision between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 10: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns watches a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 10, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images At least according to our poll, Cleveland Browns fans feel confident that either they know who the starting quarterback should be already or will after the joint practice and preseason game with the Buffalo Bills: According to GM Andrew Berry (and as previously said by HC Todd Monken), the decision between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders will come down to production and production alone . A report on Saturday said that Watson came into training camp with a lead but that Sanders has impressed since arriving in Berea. Overall, the Browns offense hasn’t looked sharp so far in camp as Monken tries to balance scheme fit with the players’ talent . The Cleveland head coach gave an update on the state of the QB competition and when he expects the two to potentially separate themselves: “Doing fine. I don’t think you’re really going to know until you get through all the installs, because we’re not game planning against our own defense. Each day has been a different part of the pass game, so it’s hard to really [tell]. And one day you go with the ones, the other day you go with the twos, certainly that matchup is going to be different depending on who you’re going against. I think the most important thing is, from a process standpoint, how are we operating at the line of scrimmage, where are their eyes, have they taken command of one the huddle, and then cadence, and then understanding the concepts. I think they’re all doing good, they’re all fine. All of our players are working through mistakes and fighting like hell to get better.” Monken noted that the team is only halfway through installs at this point (four of eight days in). Near the end of his media session, the Browns head coach also gave an interesting answer about what he is evaluating at the position right now: At this point when you’re installing, when I’m scripting, I really am not scripting on who is at quarterback, they each have a different skill set, so as of right now, I’m not evaluating any of them. I’m not making a decision on any of them until we get through all the installs, and we get to where the practices are the same, we’re scripting it based on who’s taking the reps. And we’re playing the preseason games, and we’re going against the Bills. I’ll take that back. We are evaluating, but not to that extreme, nothing’s going to be decided over these install practices. We’re just getting it in, letting the guys compete, see where we’re at, that’s at all positions. Once we get further along in pads, the full install in, we get to compete against other people, that’s really when I’m going to be able to see it because I haven’t coached any of these four quarterbacks until now, I haven’t been around them. I don’t have any preconceived notions of who they’ve been or where they’re going. I just take it day to day, we install, and as we get further along, we’ll have a better idea.” Anyone expecting a quick quarterback decision in Cleveland/Berea might be in for a far different outcome, based on Monken’s comments. What do you think about Monken’s comments about the QB competition and his process overall so far? Do you think it is taking far too long, or is the Browns coach doing the right thing by taking his time? Join the conversation! title: Browns QB competition: Watson came in with ‘leg up,’ Shedeur has ‘upward trajectory’
summary: The Cleveland Browns QB competition is the story of the team’s training camp, even if it might be overblown by many fans and media. GM Andrew Berry and HC Todd Monken have made it clear that the only thing that matters is who produces the best between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders, despite the latter’s […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JULY 30: Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns looks to pass as Deshaun Watson #4 throws a pass during the Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on July 30, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns QB competition is the story of the team’s training camp, even if it might be overblown by many fans and media. GM Andrew Berry and HC Todd Monken have made it clear that the only thing that matters is who produces the best between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders , despite the latter’s age and potential development. Sanders has been taking on some leadership and mentorship responsibility with rookie QB Taylen Green and could really benefit from adding a quick deep ball to his arsenal , according to one analyst. Watson, on the other hand, is hoping to have a bounce-back season some six years after his last quality play. Heading into training camp, Watson reportedly had the lead in the quarterback competition . That was reiterated by The NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, live from Berea, but the long-time reporter also noted the positives seen from Sanders, something noted by team reporter Nathan Zegura this offseason as well: From Back Together Weekend, live from Cleveland: The #Browns QB battle is in focus. pic.twitter.com/VQO8yspZUg — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 1, 2026 While there has been noted concern about the Browns offense so far in training camp, including by Monken, who noted the team’s defense is making things tough for their counterparts , improvement from Sanders could push things to another level. title: Browns: 3 takeaways from ownership about the current state of the team
summary: One of the highlights of summer in Northeast Ohio is the opening of training camp for the Cleveland Browns. After six long months without football, the sight of those orange helmets, daily quarterback trackers, and hearing from the coaches and players about mostly meaningful topics is always welcome.  Then there is the annual media day […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 09: Managing and principal partner Jimmy Haslam of the Cleveland Browns watches a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 09, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images One of the highlights of summer in Northeast Ohio is the opening of training camp for the Cleveland Browns. After six long months without football, the sight of those orange helmets, daily quarterback trackers, and hearing from the coaches and players about mostly meaningful topics is always welcome. Then there is the annual media day where ownership talks about expectations for the season and, to some extent, shares the overall feeling about the current state of the franchise. That took place on Friday, with Jimmy Haslam joined by managing partner JW Johnson to chat about the team. Here are three takeaways from what they had to say. Cautiously optimistic about this season The Browns enter the season with low expectations on a national level , with the belief that they will once again be one of the league’s worst teams, as sportsbooks have pegged the over/under at 5.5 wins . He may not be a betting man, league rules and all, but Haslam said he would take the over as he has high hopes for the Browns in 2026 : “I just want to say we’re not punting on this season by any means. ’27 is great, but we have high expectations for this team. We had a lot of opportunities last year to win more games, and we didn’t, but this year is by no means a punt whatsoever. We’re excited about how we’re going to play; we’ll see how the schedule shakes out, but the guys are ready to win this year. There’s no mandate like, ‘hey we just have to focus on ’27 and beyond.’ Every year we want to win. “We’re always careful, as you know, to set the expectations, and I think we’ve made giant strides in our talent level the last few years. It takes these young guys a lot of time, and I think we could have a chance to start double-digit first- and second-year players. I don’t care how good you are, it takes a little bit of time to improve. But we’re really excited about the roster we’ve assembled.” A hard coach for a hard job The Browns interviewed several candidates during their head coach search to replace Kevin Stefanski, who led the team to the playoffs twice in his six seasons. That search ultimately landed on the 60-year-old Todd Monken, making him an NFL head coach for the first time. The combination of Monken’s skill on offense and his ability to embrace being both a coach and a teacher made him the top choice, according to Haslam : “What’s interesting is Todd was here for a year, so we got to know him pretty well, and the three years that he was at Baltimore, for whatever reason, we stayed in contact, and always thought very highly of him. (Todd) coaches really hard, and he coaches the players hard, and he coaches the coaches hard. If you’re the wide receiver coach and some guy runs eight yards shorter than that, you’re going to hear about it right then — you might not wait until after practice. This is coaching and teaching, and I think he’s really good at it and really comfortable at it. “I think Todd’s comfortable in his own skin. I don’t want to share trade secrets, but he was my favorite from the get-go. We had some good coaches, and people drop out, and people don’t turn out the way you thought, but he was my pick from the first. Everybody says he’s never been a head coach, and he’s 60, but we had the choice of taking that or somebody who’s never been a head coach and is 32 or 33. So, I like that.” The quarterbacks. Always the quarterbacks. It would not be summer in Cleveland without a training camp battle to see who will be the starting quarterback , even if that person only lasts a few games. This is also the final year of Deshaun Watson’s five-year contract, and while there has been talk that the reaction of the fans will sway Monken’s decision, Johnson said that is not going to be a factor : “I think everyone’s a fan of each guy; some like Deshuan, a lot of people don’t, some people like Shedeur (Sanders), maybe some people don’t. It really doesn’t matter, and those guys don’t care about it. As we said earlier, those guys have been here working hard. All they want to do is win and help this team out. They know our success on the field is paramount for the team, our fans, our organization, and for this city. “Having eight wins in the last two years is unacceptable … we had a ton of opportunities last year to win more games, and we just didn’t. But we feel comfortable about those guys. Whoever wins the job, we’re going to support them, and we hope the fans do too. The best thing they can do is play well and win football games, and that’ll change the narrative.” Haslam followed up with possibly the truest thing he has ever said as owner of the Browns : “I think one thing I’ve noticed about fans is that if a player plays well, they tend to come around.” Those are some of the takeaways from the media session. Now it’s your turn. Here is the full transcript – what stood out to you the most? Let everyone know in the comments!

title: Browns GM Andrew Berry refuses to follow Sashi Brown’s, other failed regimes’ processes
summary: In many ways, Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry’s resume can be separated by what happened before the 2025 NFL draft (specifically the Deshaun Watson trade, which led to moving on from Baker Mayfield) and everything that has happened since the start of that draft. Before the 2025 draft, Berry made a lot of moves to […]
full_text: BEREA, OH - JANUARY 21, 2016: Executive vice president of football operations Sashi Brown of the Cleveland Browns listens during an introductory press conference on January 21, 2016 at the Cleveland Browns training facility in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images/Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images In many ways, Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry’s resume can be separated by what happened before the 2025 NFL draft (specifically the Deshaun Watson trade , which led to moving on from Baker Mayfield ) and everything that has happened since the start of that draft. Before the 2025 draft, Berry made a lot of moves to try to open up and create a Super Bowl window for the Browns. Since that draft, the moves have been far more about the future than the present: Traded down from the #2 pick ( Travis Hunter ) Traded down from the #6 pick Traded away Myles Garrett The haul in return for Hunter and Garrett combined to give Cleveland a huge set of draft assets and talent. Berry, unlike his former Browns boss Sashi Brown and other Cleveland front office executives, has also refused to go scorched earth on the roster. Under Brown, the Browns roster was stripped to its foundations with only young and cheap players left. The idea was to bottom out as much as possible in order to get as high of draft picks and develop the young players selected with those picks. During Berry’s introductory press conference back in 2020, the young exec made it clear that he would be distancing himself from the “tanking” business of the past Browns front office he worked for. Quite often during that media session, Berry used the word “aggressive” to describe his plans, including in talent acquisition: “If we go back a little bit to what I talked about earlier, we are not going to limit ourselves to one method of player acquisition. If we can be targeted and strategic on the free agent market, we are going to be aggressive there. If there is anything that I want to be defined by, it is aggression. We want to aggressively acquire talent because that is the name of the game from an NFL front office perspective, and we are going to explore every avenue that enables us to do that.” While his moves prior to the 2025 draft have been hit and miss, including the big miss with Watson, Berry has stayed true to his word by being aggressive. Since 2025, he’s also been aggressive in making moves to set up the team’s future but, unlike Brown and others, has valued keeping talent on the roster. This offseason alone, three decisions show the big difference between Berry and other front offices as they were looking to rebuild: Required Jared Verse , not more draft capital, in the Garrett trade Extended Denzel Ward Extended Grant Delpit On top of that, Berry made it clear this week that production, not age and contract , will decide whether Watson or Shedeur Sanders will be the team’s starting quarterback this season. Under Brown and others, Sanders would be locked into that spot due to his youth and rookie contract. There is still a long way to go to find out if Berry’s method of rebuilding Cleveland’s roster will work or not. One thing is crystal clear, however, and that is that the Browns general manager has no plans to strip that roster bare, no plans to tank a season, and no plans to do anything but continue to be aggressive.
