title: Cowboys news: Dallas o-line elite in one area, suspect in another
summary: Cowboys offensive line praise comes with one unavoidable condition – Marcus Mosher, The Landry Hat The praise that comes at a price. No team in the NFL has invested more into their offensive line than the Dallas Cowboys over the last five years. The Cowboys have spent three first-round picks on the unit since the […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 14: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) backs into the pocket behind his offensive line during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Minnesota Vikings on December 14, 2025 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Cowboys offensive line praise comes with one unavoidable condition – Marcus Mosher, The Landry Hat The praise that comes at a price. No team in the NFL has invested more into their offensive line than the Dallas Cowboys over the last five years. The Cowboys have spent three first-round picks on the unit since the 2022 draft and have used another third-round choice (Cooper Beebe) on their starting center. There are several teams across the league who have not taken a single first-round offensive lineman in the last decade, let alone three in five years. But the Cowboys believe their offensive line, specifically their interior offensive line , can be the strength of their team. The truth is, it better be, considering all of the resources and assets they’ve used to address the group. Despite all of the resources spent, this has not been an elite unit over the last few years. However, Dallas is hopeful that it will change in 2026. In a recent article by offensive line expert Brandon Thorn, he ranked all 32 offensive lines heading into the NFL over on Establish The Run . The Cowboys did make an appearance inside the top 10, coming in at No. 9. Thorn also joined the Locked On Cowboys Podcast recently and mentioned that he would have ranked this unit higher if the rankings weren’t slanted toward pass protection over run blocking (Establish The Run is a fantasy football website, and his OL rankings are weighted more towards passing). Tyler Guyton will determine the ceiling of the Cowboys’ talented offensive line One of the reasons why Thorn was so optimistic about the Cowboys’ offensive line this year was due to the interior offensive linemen on the roster, including Tyler Smith and Tyler Booker. This has a chance to be the best guard duo in all of the league, and if Cooper Beebe can continue to develop (Thorn is high on Beebe), there is no reason they can’t dominate upfront. Comparing the 2 Dallas Cowboys linebacker options – Mark Heaney, Inside the Star The Cowboys could fortify their young linebacker group with either one of these veteran choices. Training camp may be underway, but the main story following America’s Team this past week was the front office alluding to additional roster moves being made. Owner and General Manager Jerry Jones made it clear that Dallas is still in the trade market, and an addition to the Cowboys linebacker room makes the most sense. Sure, Maxx Crosby could also make sense, but I think Dallas is comfortable with their EDGE room, at least for now. In my eyes, that leaves the linebacker position as the most likely place they are thinking of adding to. It was their worst group last season, and while Dee Winters and Jaishawn Barham are nice additions, they could use a true top dog in the room. Two options in particular stand out, and that’s what we’ll get into here; this is a quick overview and comparison between free agent Bobby Wagner and Dolphins star Jordyn Brooks. Bobby Wagner Overview: Long-Time NFL Veteran Still Produces (36 Y/O, 162 Total Tackles for Washington in 2025, All-Pro in 2024). “B-Wags” has been filling up the tackle sheet in the NFL since 2012, and this is the first time he has really been left without a team. The 36-year-old former Seahawk, Ram, and Commander, has been rumored to be a Cowboys target for a long time, but this seems like the first real chance at it becoming a reality. Wagner’s 11-year All-Pro streak (insane stat right there) was broken last season, as his numbers took a slight downturn and his actual performance did seem like that of a nearly 40-year-old linebacker. The speed and quickness just isn’t as elite as it once was. Still, he’s a fantastic IQ and locker room player, productive, and would clearly be a starter for Dallas. He isn’t a long-term fix like Brooks, but he is a logical low-cost band-aid on a big issue for Dallas. Tough news about the Cowboys’ most double-teamed defensive linemen – Reid Hanson, Cowboys Wire The numbers don’t lie. Despite posting a league-leading 31.2 pressure rate, the Dallas Cowboys only ranked 22nd in actual sack production. With Micah Parsons no longer demanding double-teams in Dallas, offenses feasted against the Cowboys’ struggling pass rush. For years, Parsons demanded all the attention, absorbing double-teams and making life easier on his teammates in the process. Without Parsons, everyone had to do their part. The thing about double-teams is that they’re unavoidable. Most plays, the numbers are engineered to work in an offense’s favor, so someone has to face it. In 2025 it was a surprising collection of defenders who had the highest double-team rate for the Cowboys and unfortunately two of those players are no longer in Dallas here in 2026. As hard as it is to believe, the Cowboy who demanded the highest double-team rate was Solomon Thomas. Based on PFF play tracking, Thomas’ 67.40 double-team percentage was 12 th in the NFL. For a guy that only played 227 pass rush snaps that’s pretty good. Thomas moved on to the Tennessee Titans over the offseason and no longer factors into the Cowboys’ equation this year. The second most double-teamed lineman in Dallas was Kenny Clark. His production might have dipped in 2025 but respect from offenses remain intact. Clark is back in 2026, but his role in Christian Parker’s system is a source of concern. Clark may have to man the nose tackle spot in the 3-4 if other options don’t work out. It will guarantee a heavy dose of doubles but will take a chunk out of his pressures in the process. In his time split between the New York Jets and the Cowboys, Quinnen Williams was double-teamed at a rate of 65.6 percent. It’s not far off from the league leaders and he saw a good deal of success through it all. Great things are expected of him in 2026, so he represents the hope for the new season. The fourth Cowboy defender on the list is Osa Odighizuwa. Like Thomas, he’s no longer with the team and will need to be replaced internally. It just so happens Odighizuwa was chipped at a higher rate than the previous three, but he typically posted good numbers as an interior pass rusher despite it all. Interior players dominated the list. It shouldn’t be surprising since the nature of their technique almost guarantees high double-team numbers. Good interior players who demand attention means edge players get to operate in space more often. It seems to be the blueprint of the Cowboys’ roster but requires dominant and feared interior players to make it work. Jerry Jones offered surprising update on curtains at Cowboys games – R.J. Ochoa, Blogging the Boys Let there (not) be light. Finally. We all know the drill by now. Around the third quarter of the afternoon games at AT&T Stadium… it happens. The time of year means that the sun shines through the glass of the building and provides lighting that makes for incredible photographs and pieces of art. Cool. None of that matters relative to the objective that the building is supposed to serve, though. At least the primary objective. Many a Cowboys player have complained about the sun and its glare through the building, and at every turn Jerry Jones has said that he isn’t doing anything about it. Jerry spoke to Mike Doocy on Saturday and said that the Cowboys were giving a thought to tinting the windows the way that FIFA did for the World Cup matches that the building hosted this summer (you know, the ones at “Dallas Stadium”). It is worth noting that the afternoon sun and the impact it has on the building is different in June than October, but the point is/was that FIFA did not take a chance that the play on the field would be compromised. Obviously Jerry…

It is worth noting that the afternoon sun and the impact it has on the building is different in June than October, but the point is/was that FIFA did not take a chance that the play on the field would be compromised. Obviously Jerry saying that the Cowboys were simply thinking about this is not the same thing as legitimate action being taken; however, anyone who has followed the team and this storyline for some time knows that Jerry has historically completely shut down any talk of this kind. That he is even remotely open to some sort of change feels worth talking about at the very least. Could we really see the Cowboys add curtains and in the process do something that can help their football team? This offseason and start to training camp has all felt like such a dream… maybe this is part of that.

title: Christian Parker has quickly instilled confidence in Cowboys defense
summary: The Dallas Cowboys defense is searching for answers on the training fields of Oxnard, California, and doing so with a new defensive coordinator for the fourth season in a row, going from the final year of Dan Quinn in 2023 to Mike Zimmer in 2024, Matt Eberflus last season, and now Christian Parker. The offense […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys defense is searching for answers on the training fields of Oxnard, California, and doing so with a new defensive coordinator for the fourth season in a row, going from the final year of Dan Quinn in 2023 to Mike Zimmer in 2024, Matt Eberflus last season, and now Christian Parker. The offense in general has had the advantage in these two practices because the pads have not been on, but the defense from a coaching perspective under Parker already feels night and day different compared to last season’s disaster with Eberflus. Take this early example between Parker and linebacker Demarvion Overshown from Thursday’s practice as likely the best example from the two sessions so far. During team periods, the defense was trying to shut down a potent Cowboys offense when the coaching staff got a little fancy. Right in the middle of a crucial pre-snap sequence, Overshown’s radio went dead. It wasn’t a glitch or his battery dying. It was pure sabotage. The coaches purposely cut the communication line to see how his linebacker would handle himself. No communication. No problem. With the time winding down and the offense shifting into formation, Overshown did not panic. No distress signals to the sideline. Instead, he took complete command of the situation. He got into the exact call he was supposed to. He had gone through this repeated times with the coaches in meetings, so there was no need to improvise. He knew exactly what he needed to do. By the time the ball was snapped, the entire unit was perfectly aligned, ready for action. on DeMarvion Overshown: in the #Cowboys first practice, Christian Parker pretended his headset went out (but Overshown thought he was serious — CP and Schotty having planned the deception to test his green dot ability). "Overshown immediately made the right [play] call." — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) July 30, 2026 It doesn’t feel like a stretch at all to say that something like this wasn’t even in the realm of possibility for the Cowboys defense in 2025 with their communication problems. Furthermore, for Parker to be new on the scene with the memory of this historically bad defense still fresh in everyone’s mind, and have the confidence on day two to throw something like this at Overshown and the defense as a whole is easy confirmation of all the things the Cowboys have been saying about Parker from the start. Confidence, communication, and a mastery of scheme teaching were all things the Cowboys believed they found in Parker when hiring him at the end of their most exhaustive DC search in quite a while, and those things are coming through already from the coach Schotty called the “hardest working coach he’s ever been around” . The other dynamic that Parker brings is the return of a true iron sharpening iron feel to practices between the Cowboys offense and defense, which uplifts the entire competitive nature of the team. The Cowboys were certainly missing this last year, and really haven’t had such a dynamic since Quinn was defensive coordinator. The early returns on how this is working out in Oxnard for 2026 between Schottenheimer and Parker have Cowboys fans fired up. The two coaches talking in press conference settings about the trash talk they have on the field when calling plays against one another is one thing. Seeing it come to life in practices where George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb are getting the best of this defense in one segment, and in others the secondary players guarding them like Cobie Durant and DaRon Bland holding their own, is another thing entirely that adds to the excitement of what this team can be come gamedays. The Cowboys organization has simply not had a strong enough defense in any recent seasons to be considered real contenders, even when Dak Prescott and the offense were leading the world in many offensive categories. The best part about this potentially shifting under Parker is that the move came in time to see the offensive talent still in place, so much so in fact that all 11 starters are back on this side of the ball. This is naturally still where the Dallas front office is looking to base their entire evaluation of the team around, making it so Stephen Jones seeing the defense giving Prescott and the offense problems another really good sign. Stephen Jones said on @1053thefan that he's spent a lot of time in the #Cowboys ' defensive meeting room to get a feel for Christian Parker, his staff and their interactions amongst themselves and their players. “It’s been really interesting. Like you said, it’s early, but I do… — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) July 31, 2026 National reporter Albert Breer was at the start of Cowboys camp earlier this week, and reported back on the overall culture that Schottenheimer has put in place, something that Parker getting the defense back up to a standard is fitting in with nicely. When Breer mentioned the players the Cowboys have acquired that have also helped bring along this culture, he immediately went to Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, and Jalen Thompson. . @AlbertBreer visited the #Cowboys this week, and one of his takeaways was that the added leadership on the roster has been noticeable. “…Dak [Prescott] has had to be the voice for that locker room for a long time, and there have been moments this offseason when the leadership… pic.twitter.com/qURn49C4eH — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) August 1, 2026 His overall point started with Prescott, but still, when was the last time the Cowboys were viewed as having cornerstone players at defensive tackle (two of them!) and safety. A safety that actually paid for in free agency, which is just one of several moves that show a personnel commitment to giving Parker the right pieces to work with, something they didn’t remotely do with Eberflus as DC a year ago. Ultimately, it will be about these “Jimmies and Joes” and not all about the “Xs and Os” brought to the defense by Parker that help the Cowboys decide games with more than just their offense and special teams this season, and seeing new acquisitions pick up on coaching quickly to stand out already is heartening. Caleb Downs was expected to make a splash early and has done so as the 11th overall pick brought in as a perfect fit for what the Cowboys are looking for in the secondary at nickel. There has not been quite as much buzz about fellow first-round pick Malachi Lawrence, but that goes for the defensive line as a whole going through drills without full contact right now. Both are expected to see the field as rookies, but that expectation doesn’t end here with the two first-rounders. Third-round pick Jaishawn Barham has made an early impression and is handling being used in multiple spots of the defense well. For the Cowboys to truly pull off a one year turnaround from the worst defense to a contending one, it’s going to take this level of contributions from everyone they’ve acquired, and that appears to be firmly in Christian Parker’s plan through this training camp and preseason. While the offense has shown right from the gun in Oxnard that the Cowboys defense will likely only need to be middle of the pack for this team to improve in the win column for 2026, the defense has had their own say in the edge and attention to detail they want to play with under Parker to be a force that can win games on their own as well.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 43
summary: It is Day 43 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: 10 Nov 1996: Defensive lineman Leon Lett of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during a game against the San Francisco 49ers at 3Com Park in San Francisco, California. The Cowboys won the game in overtime, 20-17. Mandatory Credit: Al Bello /Allsport | Getty Images It is Day 43 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Welcome back as we get to Day 43 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit another chapter in what was unquestionably the NFL’s premier rivalry of the 1990s. By the time the Cowboys traveled to Candlestick Park in Week 11 of the 1996 season, Dallas and San Francisco had met in the previous four NFC Championship Games, splitting them two apiece. Even though this was a regular-season matchup, it carried the feel of January football. Sunday, November 10, 1996 — 4:00 p.m. ET 3Com Park, San Francisco, California Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 20, San Francisco 49ers 17 (Overtime) San Francisco controlled the first quarter. Jeff Wilkins opened the scoring with a 28-yard field goal, then Steve Young found Iheanyi Uwaezuoke for a 29-yard touchdown. The 49ers led 10-0, while Dallas struggled to establish Emmitt Smith or generate any consistent rhythm against one of the league’s strongest defenses. The Cowboys finally responded late in the second quarter. Troy Aikman finished a lengthy drive by scrambling three yards for a touchdown with 32 seconds remaining before halftime. That cut San Francisco’s lead to 10-7 and gave Dallas something tangible from a first half in which the 49ers had largely dictated the game. The matchup changed when Young was knocked out after taking multiple sacks from the Dallas defence. He had completed seven of 13 passes for 83 yards and the early touchdown before Elvis Grbac took over. Grbac had tormented Dallas in San Francisco’s 38-20 win at Texas Stadium the previous season, but this time the Cowboys pressured him into mistakes. Only four seconds had elapsed in the fourth quarter when Chris Boniol made a 26-yard field goal to tie the game at 10 points. But San Francisco immediately answered. Terry Kirby broke loose for a 27-yard touchdown run, restoring the 49ers’ seven-point lead with 11:38 remaining. Dallas was back in the same position it had occupied for most of the afternoon, chasing San Francisco in a stadium where the Cowboys’ dynasty had produced some of its greatest moments. Aikman appeared to be leading the tying drive when Dallas reached the San Francisco red zone, but Marquez Pope intercepted him in the end zone with around six and a half minutes remaining. It could have ended the Cowboys’ comeback. Instead, Dallas’ defense handed the opportunity straight back. On San Francisco’s next offensive play, linebacker Fred Strickland intercepted Grbac near the 49ers’ goal line. Three plays later, Aikman found Eric Bjornson for a six-yard touchdown. Boniol’s extra point tied the game at 17 with 2:45 left. A drive that had seemingly died with Pope’s interception had been revived by one defensive play and finished by Dallas’ replacement for the injured Jay Novacek. Dallas won the overtime coin toss and did not give the ball back. Aikman completed all five of his passes on a controlled 12-play, 66-yard possession, while Smith helped grind the Cowboys into scoring range. Boniol then made a 29-yard field goal to end the game, completing a comeback from 10 points down and giving Dallas its first victory over San Francisco since the 1993 NFC Championship Game. This game belongs on the countdown because it was a major course correction in the Cowboys’ final season as a serious championship-era contender. Dallas had begun the year 1-3 and entered this game fighting to remain relevant in the NFC East. Beating a 7-2 San Francisco team on the road showed that the ageing core could still win a physical, high-pressure game against the rival that had defined its decade. The Cowboys eventually finished 10-6, won their fifth consecutive NFC East title and reached the divisional round. #Cowboys vs #49ers 1996 Week 11 Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 20, San Francisco 49ers 17 (Overtime) #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/QeM9IAK09o — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) July 31, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Young and Grbac combined for only 171 passing yards. Grbac completed 10 of 17 passes for 88 yards but threw interceptions to Strickland and Woodson. title: 3 questions after the first two days of Cowboys training camp
summary: The Dallas Cowboys wereoff on Friday, which means it’s a good time to take stock of where the team stands. There’s not a ton of critical information to pull from just 48 hours of practice time, but the trends are starting to develop on both sides of the ball. Here are three questions we’re left […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker (left) with head coach Brian Schottenheimer at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys wereoff on Friday, which means it’s a good time to take stock of where the team stands. There’s not a ton of critical information to pull from just 48 hours of practice time, but the trends are starting to develop on both sides of the ball. Here are three questions we’re left with heading into the weekend around Cowboys training camp. 1. Checking the Mic After two days of camp, head coach Brian Schottenheimer sounds very confident in DeMarvion Overshown’s ability to wear the green dot on defense. Schotty said the team ran through a scenario in which the headset communication between Christian Parker and Overshown broke down . It was up to Overshown to make the right call. The Dallas head coach praised the young linebacker for getting the team in the right spot. It’s no secret the Cowboys linebacking core is a question mark right now, and it starts with who the team feels confident in to lead the defense and relay the calls on the field. Schottenheimer said there are about three or four players that will rotate the mic responsibilities as camp moves along. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said in addition to DeMarvion Overshown wearing the green dot, rookie Caleb Downs, Shemar James and Curtis Robinson are also wearing the green dot. That speaks volumes about what they think of Caleb Downs. @DLLS_Cowboys — Clarence Hill Jr (@clarencehilljr) July 30, 2026 The Cowboys could be looking to add at linebacker through a potential trade or free agent addition , so all options remain on the table for now. 2. Five is a crowd When it comes to crunching the numbers for the final roster, the Cowboys won’t need to worry about that for a few weeks. However, given what CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Ryan Flournoy have done over two days, it begs the question of whether four receivers might be enough to make the initial 53-man roster. The Cowboys might want to go longer at positions of question like defensive line or linebacker, so having a fifth wide receiver could be a luxury Dallas can’t afford. The Cowboys may have the best wide receiver trio in the NFL, and adding KaVontae Turpin into the mix as a gadget, fourth option may be enough. Jonathan Mingo, Anthony Smith, Traeshon Holden and the rest of the wide receiver room will have to be special to justify Dallas keeping a fifth wide receiver over a defensive player. 3. Rushing to conclusions After two days, if one side of the ball had to be crowned “the winner,” it would be the offense. Dak Prescott has reportedly had all day to throw in the pocket and hasn’t seen much pressure. The glass-half-full approach would say the Dallas offense will live up to the hype of ‘Greatest Offense There Is’ and the offensive line is poised to take a big step forward. The glass-half-empty approach would say the pass rush is in desperate need of help. Will Maxx Crosby be a part of the Cowboys plans for 2026? The trade that may lurk around the corner will tell a lot about the team’s confidence in where their pass rush unit may be.

For the linebacker/secondary groups, Caleb Downs is a true charting nightmare, and I hope he will have a similar effect on opposing offenses. title: 2 Cowboys who may have trouble grabbing a roster spot
summary: There’s no sense in cutting players after two days of training camp, but the Dallas Cowboys have a few players who are starting to pull away from the rest of the group. Heading into camp, one of the team’s biggest concerns was who would be the RB2 behind Javonte Williams? Jaydon Blue broke off a […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Malik Davis #20 of the Dallas Cowboys runs with the ball during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s no sense in cutting players after two days of training camp, but the Dallas Cowboys have a few players who are starting to pull away from the rest of the group. Heading into camp, one of the team’s biggest concerns was who would be the RB2 behind Javonte Williams? Jaydon Blue broke off a long run in the team’s first practice and showcased why his breakaway speed made him an appealing prospect in the first place. Phil Mafah has also already had a few highlights in practice Players need to see their practice reps go up between now and the first preseason matchup, and need a few splash plays along the way. Here are a couple of names that need some action to help make the roster. Malik Davis, RB Jaydon Blue breaking out into the open for the second day in a row pic.twitter.com/vsJv4CXmqi — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) July 30, 2026 Keeping with the running back conversation, Malik Davis had a career year with Dallas last year, which should have earned him enough to be the unquestioned No. 2 back to start camp. Instead, Blue and Phil Mafah are seeing a lot more action. Davis came back to Dallas at the very end of camp last year and was able to play in a preseason game with little practice time. That impressed Schottenheimer and the coaching staff. However, if the team is looking at the long-term picture for the position group, Davis might not fit into the equation given the flexibility of rookie contracts with Mafah and Blue. There were enough eyes on Davis’ production last season that could lure some trade interest from other teams. Maybe the Cowboys can pull off an end-of-training-camp trade for a position of need. If Dallas feels like they could do a player-for-player swap, maybe Davis could be someone who gets the front office what they’re looking for, and he can go compete for meaningful snaps elsewhere. The running back rotation will be an interesting storyline to follow all of camp. Phil Mafah goes untouched on this outside carry #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/XrZ4Nwttcn — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) July 30, 2026 Shemar James, LB The hype around Jaishawn Barham is real. The 2026 third-round pick has looked solid across two days of practice and is excelling starting out as an off-ball linebacker. One player who could be in danger of making the 53 might be Shemar James. Barham was already in the plans for this season, but his presence alone pushes James further down the depth chart. Combine that with the new coaching staff, and things look a little different for James than they did a season ago. With Christian Parker in the fold, he went out and added Barham, traded for Dee Winters, and signed Curtis Robinson back in April. Three new linebackers who could end up fitting what Parker’s vision of the defense is supposed to look like, leaving James as the odd man out. Brian Schottenheimer has also praised Justin Barron for what he’s seen in his development, so the final linebacker spot could be a fight between James and Barron. Or, James could lose out to an unnamed veteran who may be brought in. Stephen and Jerry Jones seem to have trades or veteran free agents on their mind to improve the defense. If they grab a veteran LB, James could be the guy pushed out. It’s not all bad for James. The team leader in tackles a season ago still has a ton of time left to show his ability to grow under a new staff. Preseason games are made for linebackers looking to find their way either on defense or special teams. The question is whether James can overcome all of the change on defense and the loss of the one spokesperson in Eberflus who championed for him during draft weekend. (Obvious caveats of no pads and first practice) I loved seeing this rep from the DAL defense. Kenny Clark recognizes the screen quickly and forces the RB to stop his feet and cut back right into Jaishawn Barham, who took an aggressive angle to back door Tyler Booker. Bland also… pic.twitter.com/GjD8t3ejUe — John Owning (@JohnOwning) July 30, 2026

title: Denver Broncos roster review: Tight end Adam Trautman
summary: Adam Trautman is another Sean Payton guy. He was drafted by the Saints in 2020 and headed to Denver in 2023. He’s a reliable tight end who can do a little bit of everything that the position requires. He’s been talked about mostly as a blocking tight end. That being said, he’s a guy who […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Adam Trautman #82 of the Denver Broncos exits the field at halftime during an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Adam Trautman is another Sean Payton guy. He was drafted by the Saints in 2020 and headed to Denver in 2023. He’s a reliable tight end who can do a little bit of everything that the position requires. He’s been talked about mostly as a blocking tight end. That being said, he’s a guy who caught the ball when needed as a reliable target for Nix in the past couple of years, which is the reason the team signed him to an extension this offseason. Player Profile Adam Trautman | Tight End | Denver Broncos Height: 6′ 5″ Weight: 253 pounds Age: 29 years old Experience: 7th season College: Dayton 2025 stats: 20 catches for 195 yards, 1 TD Contract 2026 outlook with the Broncos Trautman is the one guy in the tight end room that has no question marks around him over the next two seasons at least. He’s a team player, knows the playbook in and out, is a willing run blocker, and can catch down the seam or on the sideline in a pinch. He’s got the history of run blocking under his belt, but seems fairly average to me at the actual job. I tend to think that is because he’s developed into a reliable pass catcher to round out what he does. This offense doesn’t need a true road-grading 285lb tight end to keep the run game moving. It does need a guy like Trautman who can do either aspect of the job at an average or above-average level at times so that they can stay on schedule or extend drives. Trautman may not be the flashiest of tight ends, but he’s the kind of reliable starter every NFL coach wants in the room. Final Word The biggest value I see in him on the team is as a veteran resource that is going to help the tight end room develop talent. Young players like Caleb Logner, Justin Joly, and Dallen Bently will be able to learn from him as the season wears on and have an excellent example of how to go about the business of being a professional tight end in this league. That’s not to say I don’t think he’s a good player. He is. He’s not the high-ceiling tight end this roster is yearning for (and has been for years, honestly). He wasn’t paid like that because both he and the Broncos know what his fit is on this team.

title: Broncos target 2027 groundbreaking for new stadium
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Look for the Denver Broncos to break ground on their new stadium in 2027. At least that’s according to Broncos president Damani Leech after meeting with the media on Saturday prior to training camp practice. That would allow the franchise to meet its goal of completion in four years. Leech said […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JUNE 18 : Burnham Yard photographed in Denver, Colorado on Thursday, June 18, 2026. (Photo by Hyoung Chang/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Look for the Denver Broncos to break ground on their new stadium in 2027. At least that’s according to Broncos president Damani Leech after meeting with the media on Saturday prior to training camp practice. That would allow the franchise to meet its goal of completion in four years. Leech said the groundbreaking goal is late spring or early summer of next year. The common theme remains now as it has throughout the process: The Broncos are taking a thoughtful approach and not rushing anything. “We feel like 2031 is still achievable for sure,” Leech said to the media. “Again, everybody has to be involved. Certainly, there’s things that we have to do and deliver to city council, but there’s other groups that are participating in the process in order to make that happen and make it a reality, but we think it’s realistic and achievable.” The Broncos are “laser focused” on opening their new stadium at Burnham Yard in 2031, per Damani Leech. Believes it’s still a realistic timeline. Burnham Yard is still the “preferred site” pic.twitter.com/S3k2YqlleJ — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 1, 2026 For now, Burnham Yard remains the “ preferred site ,” as it has for about a year. For Burnham to just be the site, Leech said, it’s beyond the Broncos’ control. In May, the franchise made a major step with the purchase agreement for Burnham Yard. “Ultimately, it goes to, when does city council approve all of those things?” he said on Saturday. “So you have to have a community benefits agreement signed, take that to city council, they approve our development agreement, they approve our rezoning agreement. There’s a number of agreements that have to be approved by city council. “If we move forward with DURA and tax increment financing, all of those things have to be approved by city council. Ideally, those would be approved right around the same time, and once that happens, I think that’s a good indicator we’ve moved off a preferred site.” In the meantime, the franchise has chosen an architect for the new stadium. If the new headquarters are an indication, the stadium will be a masterpiece. “We’ve been working with Manica, a global, world-renowned architecture firm, for a number of months now, and continue to progress on designs of the stadium,” Leech said. “I think the things that we’ve seen have been pretty beautiful. Greg and Carrie are very, very involved, have a great relationship with David and his team, and things are going well there. “Our master plan continues to iterate and evolve. Sasaki (an architecture, planning, landscape, and design firm) got us to a really great point. We’ve brought on Tryba Architects, which is a local Denver-based firm that’s done a lot of great work here in Denver to help us continue to evolve that master plan. “We look forward to sharing updated renders of that here in the very near future and stadium renders, when it’s ready, will be shared probably on a much longer-term timeline, but (I) look forward to sharing in the very near future some updated renders of the district and neighborhood master plan.” For those curious, yes, it appears the Broncos will go with the PSL route for the new stadium. That’s a private seat license, or fee, that gives you the right to purchase season tickets. “As you know, I think every stadium in the last 10-plus years that’s been built, there have been PSLs issued,” Leech said. “So it seems like it’s a pretty likely thing to happen, but we haven’t made any formal decisions on that.” Ultimately, the goal of the new stadium is to host the Super Bowl. “It’s certainly something that’s on our minds,” Leech said. “It’s on the mayor’s mind, the governor’s mind, I think, fans as well. I wouldn’t say it’s a thing that we think about every day. We do understand that the league is pretty prescriptive about how they award those well into the future, so it’s definitely something worth thinking about. Obviously, we’ve got to get into the stadium and operate it for at least a couple of years before we can play a Super Bowl, but I would love to host the Super Bowl.”

title: Bo Nix says he’s ahead of where he was last year
summary: The injury to Bo Nix will always trigger some sort of PTSD. The highest of highs, followed by the lowest of lows. What could have been? Until he plays a regular-season game, all eyes will be on Nix. It’ll also lead to questions about how it’ll impact his play for the Denver Broncos. The Broncos […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, CO - JULY 31: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos throws a pass during training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on July 31, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The injury to Bo Nix will always trigger some sort of PTSD. The highest of highs, followed by the lowest of lows. What could have been? Until he plays a regular-season game, all eyes will be on Nix . It’ll also lead to questions about how it’ll impact his play for the Denver Broncos. The Broncos quarterback has taken the first steps post-ankle injury by taking the field at training camp. And through the first two days of camp , he hasn’t missed a beat. Nix is tossing bombs and dimes to receivers and running backs. As Luca Evans put on social media, Nix looks “considerably better + more poised + accurate two days into 2026 camp than at this time in 2025 camp.” Take this with a grain of salt, but an objective observation: Bo Nix looks considerably better + more poised + accurate two days into 2026 camp than at this time in 2025 camp https://t.co/p3nHM2O3tA — Luca Evans (@bylucaevans) August 1, 2026 For those concerned that Nix wouldn’t be the same after his ankle injury, they can exhale. As he said to the media after practice on Saturday: “I feel great. I feel normal. Nothing’s holding me back. I’m out there playing like I normally do and feel really good in my spot. I’m going to continue to push it and progress, and also continue to physically get ready for this long season. Right now, I’m exactly where I want to be for our plan, and actually was a little bit ahead of where I was last year going into the season, going into the summer. I feel really good, feel like I’m in a good spot. I think it’s showing on the field.” For those curious whether the injury will change how Nix plays and what he does on the field, he emphatically ended that discussion. Specifically, if Nix has thought about not running quite as much. “Absolutely not. I’m going to roll, and I’m going to be as athletic as I can be,” Nix said to the media. “Like the earlier question, it’s a strength of ours, and we have to use our strengths. For me, that’s when I feel at my best, and that’s when I feel free. “When I’m playing like that, when I’m moving around, it’s a good thing, but at the same time, I also know what it’s like to not have that asset and have to stay in the pocket. I feel strong no matter what the play’s going to be, no matter what happens defensively, no matter what my reaction is, I feel capable of doing it.” My word. Bo Nix continues to show how good he is off schedule. In the first 11-on-11 work of the day, Nix escaped the pocket and flicked the ball deep down the field with pressure in his face. 50-yard TD. — Aric DiLalla (@AricDiLalla) August 1, 2026 The fact that Nix’s ankle injury won’t impact his ability to extend and make plays with his legs is huge for him and the Broncos offense. That’s one of the major reasons the Broncos had the success they had last season. As Broncos head coach Sean Payton said to the media on Saturday: “It’s one of his superpowers. It’s hard to sack some quarterbacks; he’s one of them. That was something you saw on college tape. In our league, when you take a sack, you just do the analytics on what your points become in that drive, or likelihood to kick a field goal, and it all drops dramatically. So it’s certainly one of his strengths.” The key for Nix is not to become too reliant on that strength, injury or not. “For me, it’s just about the balance,” he said. “It’s making the plays when they’re there, but at the same time using that creativity and skill set when it’s not. Today, always I feel like at every practice I’ve ever been in, there’s a time or two in practice that you have to move and escape and practice that dynamic play. Our guys are in tune with it, and those guys are moving around with me. It’s just all about the play’s never over, and also being smart and just making plays.” Just like anything else in life that comes with experience. As Nix enters Year Three, there are areas where he’s shown drastic growth, such as his leadership. The more he plays and practices, the more he will improve. “Year 1, I’m trying to just not mess up for the team,” Nix said. “I feel like Year 3, I’m trying to make plays for the team. It’s just quite the different feeling. It’s just a confidence-level thing. I think playing as many games as I have already, there’s hardly going to be a situation I haven’t been in. So it’s good to lead our team. “It’s good to be on a team with other solid leaders, other veteran guys who do a great job of leadership. It’s not just me out there. There are a lot of voices, and I just think we have a really good feel right now with the leadership and the guys that are responding to our leadership. We have a really good team.” Weekend work at #BroncosCamp ⚒️ pic.twitter.com/u4m6umdgX2 — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 1, 2026 Until Nix plays in the regular season and people see him, there will be some pause. At least for now, the concerns and thoughts about Nix and his injury can be put on ice. That means good things not only for Nix but also for the Broncos as they look to build off last season. “It feels like we’re heading in the right direction as a team,” Nix said. “We’re all sort of continuing to get our feet wet the first couple of days, learning some new things, and also getting back to our favorites. I think it’s been good to see everybody move around. It’s been a competitive first couple of days, offense and defense, which is what you want to see. Both sides of the ball have been making a lot of plays. It’s just a fun time right now.”

title: 2026 Denver Broncos Training Camp: Day 2 News and Notes
summary: Day 2 of Broncos Camp is in the books, and it was another fun one. It was their last practice before a day off on Sunday. However, on Monday, the pads come on, and the most important practices of camp begin, and we get to see who shines and who falls behind. Today’s practice featured […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, CO - JULY 31: Tyler Onyedim #98 of the Denver Broncos participates in training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on July 31, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Day 2 of Broncos Camp is in the books, and it was another fun one. It was their last practice before a day off on Sunday. However, on Monday, the pads come on, and the most important practices of camp begin, and we get to see who shines and who falls behind. Weekend work at #BroncosCamp ⚒️ pic.twitter.com/u4m6umdgX2 — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 1, 2026 Today’s practice featured more big plays from Bo Nix and the Broncos quarterbacks, but the defense fought back and came away feeling good at the end of practice. Looks like we may have a real competition for the backup quarterback job, or do we? Marvin Mims is making an early statement for the WR3 job with back-to-back practices with explosive plays. We also have news about the team possibly signing Taysom Hill, notes from practices, injury updates, tweets from camp, some notable quotes from Sean Payton, Brandon Jones, and Bo Nix, and more! Explosive plays continue, but the defense fights back Like on Day 1, the Broncos had multiple explosive plays during today’s training camp practice. It all started during 7-on-7s when quarterback Bo Nix threw a dime to running back RJ Harvey, who was running a wheel route that went for 20+ yards. It didn’t stop there for Nix. During the first team period, Nix extended the play and found second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant for a 40+ yard touchdown pass. Nix wasn’t the only quarterback making plays today. Jarrett Stidham had two big chunk plays today. The first came on a broken coverage where he hit Hakeem Butler for a 70-yard touchdown, and then later in practice, hit Marvin Mims Jr. for a DEEP touchdown. However, the defense was going down lightly. After the first team period, the defense stopped the offense and once again stopped them during the final move-the-ball period to end practice. So, while the offense had some fireworks, the defense proved why they are one of the best units in the entire NFL. My word. Bo Nix continues to show how good he is off schedule. In the first 11-on-11 work of the day, Nix escaped the pocket and flicked the ball deep down the field with pressure in his face. 50-yard TD. — Aric DiLalla (@AricDiLalla) August 1, 2026 Bo Nix met with the media after practice today and was asked how it feels to be back out there practicing after missing most of the offseason due to his ankle. He told reporters that “It feels great. It feels normal” and that both sides of the ball have been making plays and that “It’s just a fun time right now”. “It feels great. It feels normal. It feels like we’re heading in the right direction as a team. We’re all sort of continuing to get our feet wet the first couple of days, learning some new things and also getting back to our favorites. I think it’s been good to see everybody move around. It’s been a competitive first couple of days, offense and defense, which is what you want to see. Both sides of the ball have been making a lot of plays. It’s just a fun time right now.” The Broncos offense has started camp hot and has been making explosive plays all over the field. One player who is expected to do that a lot for this team this upcoming season is wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. Nix was asked how it has been working with Waddle thus far and what type of receiver he is. Nix stated that Waddle is an “explosive playmaker” and hyped up all the things Waddle can do and how he will benefit and impact the offense moving forward. “He’s an explosive playmaker. The guy is really good at what he does. He makes plays, he’s fast, he’s really explosive. He’s great ball in hand, he’s great going to get the ball deep, he’s great in the screen game. He can do just a lot of things. He’s very versatile. He adds an extra element to our offense, and it’s exciting. We have a lot of different weapons that we’re using, and I think top to bottom, this is just a really strong team, really good. We just have to find what works for us and find ways to utilize all our tools.” Waddle has been as advertised thus far and lined up against cornerback Pat Surtain II during today’s practice and got the better end of the former Defensive Player of the Year. While the offense wasn’t as good as they were on Day 1, they are still doing MUCH better than in years past. Typically, we are a week or so into camp and stressing “the defense has the advantage early in camp”. We’re not doing that this year and both sides have been trading blows thus far, which is what you want to see. We’ll see how things shake out when the pads come on starting on Monday. Ehlinger was the QB2 today as the backup QB competition heats up Probably the biggest story to come from today’s practice was that backup quarterback Sam Ehlinger ran with the second-team offense while Jarrett Stidham went with the third-team offense. Talks about a potential backup quarterback competition have been whispered about all offseason, and today appeared to be the first real sign of that happening. Sam Ehlinger is the second QB up in 7on7s. Jarrett Stidham third. Interesting. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 1, 2026 Ehlinger has impressed the Broncos coaches on and off the field, and it appears they wanna see if he can push Stidham for that backup role. However, Stidham isn’t going down quietly, as he had two big touchdown passes during today’s practice. The first was to a wide-open Hakeem Butler on a broken play where he went 70 yards for a touchdown. However, later in the practice, he hit Marvin Mims Jr. for a long touchdown while in tight coverage. So, while Ehlinger getting QB2 reps is noteworthy, Stidham still performed well. With all that said, Head Coach Sean Payton downplayed this and made it all sound like a non-story. He told reporters that “he wouldn’t make anything of it”. “There was nothing remarkable or anything that we discussed in a meeting, so maybe they just unfolded where… But I wouldn’t make anything into it.” Payton downplaying it is interesting, but it happened and is something we need to monitor moving forward. As I stated, Ehlinger seems like he won over the Broncos coaching staff after signing with them last year and is getting a chance to compete for that backup job. Payton spoke about Ehlinger after practice today and told reporters that they saw “immediate growth” from him last season. “I think we just sold our program and the offense. There was nothing, we could never promise anything other than… I would say this, we saw immediate growth. I think you’d have to ask him, but I think he felt like, ‘I want to continue with this offense and continue where I’m going.’ I think he felt good about it to make that decision.” Payton downplayed it, but I do think there is something happening here. As I noted, Stidham responded with two long touchdown passes today, and both players have put their best foot forward thus far. I still would be surprised if Ehlinger surpassed Stidham, but it appears he’s getting a shot to prove himself nonetheless. Marvin Mims making a strong case for WR3 The talk all offseason was about the Broncos’ competition at wide receiver for the WR3 role behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton between Marvin Mims, Troy Franklin, and Pat Bryant. While Pat Bryant has been making some plays since camp opened, the early leader appears to be Marvin Mims Jr., who has been making plays all camp and stacking good days on top of good days. Yesterday, he made multiple big plays, and today was no different. As I noted, he caught a long touchdown from Jarrett Stidham and is really making a strong case for more snaps early on in camp. Sean Payton says Marvin Mims Jr needs “More touches.” Added he says that a lot. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 1, 2026 Head Coach Sean Payton was asked about Mims after practice today, and he once again…

title: Broncos will explore bringing in TE Taysom Hill
summary: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told NFL Network’s Cynthia Frelund that they will explore bringing in former New Orleans Saints veteran tight end/quarterback/running back Taysom Hill. Hill flourished under Sean Payton with the Saints and had teams scrambling to find the next Taysom Hill every year since. Now, the soon-to-be 36-year-old tight end who […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - DECEMBER 28: Taysom Hill #7 of the New Orleans Saints looks on during the first half of the NFL 2025 game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told NFL Network’s Cynthia Frelund that they will explore bringing in former New Orleans Saints veteran tight end/quarterback/running back Taysom Hill. Broncos Coach Sean Payton told @cfrelund Cynthia Frelund and me today that the Broncos will explore bringing in free agent tight end Taysom Hill, who played for Payton with the Saints. — Steve Wyche (@wyche89) August 1, 2026 Hill flourished under Sean Payton with the Saints and had teams scrambling to find the next Taysom Hill every year since. Now, the soon-to-be 36-year-old tight end who recently said his goodbyes to the Saints is a free agent, and the team will apparently explore the idea of bringing him in. Hill, in his goodbye message, said he is still working through what comes next, and many assumed he was heading towards retirement; he still could, but a trip to Mile High could be in the cards for the do-it-all player. First, the Broncos would have to see if Hill wants to continue playing. He turns 36 years old at the end of the month and has dealt with injuries the past few seasons. If he wants to continue, it would make sense to bring him in and see what he has left in the tank. He could add depth at the tight end position, give them a goal-line option at fullback, tight end, running back, or even quarterback. The Broncos’ tight end depth is suspect at best. Veteran Adam Trautman is likely your starter, with Evan Engram, who had a great start to camp, as the main receiving threat. After that, you have a mix of Day 3 rookies and fringe roster players. So, Hill could make sense for the Broncos and give them some added depth at the position. It remains to be seen if anything comes from this, but it appears Sean Payton and the Broncos are at least exploring the idea of bringing in Taysom Hill. What do you think, Broncos Country? title: Can Michael Dieter keep his spot as a backup center?
summary: The Miami Dolphins took Michael Deiter in the 3rd round of the 2019 NFL Draft, needing him to instantly fill up a spot on their interior offensive line. He came into that year with meaningful expectations, but over the course of four years with the team he failed to meet them. While some fans wouldn’t […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TN - DECEMBER 17: Houston Texans center Michael Deiter (63) prepares to block during a game between the Tennessee Titans and Houston Texans, December 17, 2023 at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Matthew Maxey/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins took Michael Deiter in the 3rd round of the 2019 NFL Draft, needing him to instantly fill up a spot on their interior offensive line. He came into that year with meaningful expectations, but over the course of four years with the team he failed to meet them. While some fans wouldn’t necessarily call him a “bust”, many would. After starting in 15 of 16 games at left guard his rookie season, he would be made to transition to center over the offseason, and while he dressed for all 16 games, he really only saw the field as a special teamer. In 2021 he would regain a starting spot, this time as the team’s center, and he would start in eight games until he suffered a foot injury that put him on injured reserve and ended his season. It’s good to note that most people noticed a legitimate improvement in ability compared to the previous two seasons. In year four he would return to a backup role, only logging snaps on special teams. He would not have his contract extended and would then sign with the Houston Texans. In 2023 he would start 12 consecutive games at center for Houston, including two playoff games after the starting center (who was playing in replacement of the original starting center) went down with a broken leg. He then played two seasons in Washington, starting in two games in 2024 when the starting guard was injured. He signed with the Broncos in January of 2026. Player Profile Michael Deiter | Offensive Lineman | Denver Broncos Height: 6’6” Weight: 315 pounds Age: 29 years old Experience: 8th season 2026 outlook with the Broncos Deiter’s rookie contract did not play out in the way as he hoped and has now found himself squarely in a backup position, maybe for the rest of his career. But when he has been needed, he’s been a pretty good stop-gap player for these teams, especially when he was in Houston, helping protect C.J. Stroud during his Rookie-of-the-Year campaign. He will have to fight hard for a spot on this Denver roster though. One of the biggest strengths of this team is their depth at the offensive line position. You’d be hard pressed to name teams that boast a better room than Denver does. And while that’s great for the organization, for those guys on the roster bubble this means training camp might be a blood bath. And what also complicates things for Deiter is interior offensive lineman and 2024 draft pick Nick Gargiulo coming back from an ACL injury he suffered in the 2025 preseason. Gargiulo is licked by the coaching staff and likely still has a future on this team, and he can play both center and guard, like Deiter. The Broncos also already have two backup centers on the roster, primarily Alex Forsyth, but Calvin Throckmorton was on the active roster as the backup center while Forsyth was starting in place of Luke Wattenberg. Final word Michael Deiter’s abilities might be good enough to land him on the practice squad for the Broncos, but he will have a tough time competing for that spot, let alone a place on the active roster.

title: Reports: Lions rookie Jimmy Rolder out ‘a while,’ but injury not ‘severe’
summary: The Detroit Lions’ 2026 NFL Draft class has already been hit with two significant injuries. Back in the spring, fifth-round pick Kendrick Law suffered a season-ending ACL injury. And on Friday, fourth-round pick Jimmy Rolder left a training camp practice early with a leg injury. According to a report from Justin Rogers, Rolder is expected […]
full_text: Detroit Lions linebacker Jimmy Rolder (41) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions’ 2026 NFL Draft class has already been hit with two significant injuries. Back in the spring, fifth-round pick Kendrick Law suffered a season-ending ACL injury . And on Friday, fourth-round pick Jimmy Rolder left a training camp practice early with a leg injury. According to a report from Justin Rogers, Rolder is expected to be out “for a while.” As a response, the Lions opted to sign veteran Devin White to help Detroit’s linebacker room. A positive update from Jordan Schultz: Rolder will miss time, but it is not considered a “severe injury” Some additional good news for the #Lions as sources say promising rookie LB Jimmy Rolder “didn’t suffer a severe injury” — he will “miss some time,” but not major. Rolder, the former Michigan star, left practice Friday to be evaluated for a leg injury. https://t.co/kDHgIKdDaO pic.twitter.com/TJbhfTBA5W — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) August 1, 2026 It’s a tough break for Rolder, as he had a promising start to training camp. While he wasn’t likely to be a prominent feature on Detroit’s defense in his rookie season, the former Michigan linebacker was in line for a significant role on special teams. Back in the spring, Lions coaches were optimistic about how Rolder was progressing in the early stages of his NFL career. “Still has a lot of room for growth, but I’m pretty good with where he is now,” Lions linebacker coach Shaun Dion Hamilton said in June. “I just continue to challenge him day in and day out, where it’s always a learning curve for rookies coming from college football to the pros, but I’m excited to work with him, and it’s gonna be a lot of meat on the bone and a lot of things that he can grow (from) coming into training camp.” Unfortunately, it appears Rolder’s development will have to be on hold. At this point, it’s unclear just how long “a while” is, but Detroit cannot place him on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list now that training camp has started. If the Lions opt to place him on injured reserve now, his rookie season will be over. But Detroit could opt to carry him to roster cutdowns, then place him on IR, and he would only have to miss a four-game minimum. We’ll likely get more clarity on Rolder’s issue the next time Dan Campbell is scheduled to talk to the media, which is Monday morning.

In 2025, he actually finished third in the NFL in tackles with 174—just behind Detroit’s Jack Campbell. However, he has not traditionally graded out well by PFF grade. title: Discussion: Which Lions player has been the biggest surprise in camp?
summary: The Detroit Lions have banked three training camp practices so far in 2026, and after a day off on Saturday, they’ll stack another six practices in consecutive days while welcoming fans into their Allen Park training facility starting on Sunday. For the most part, things have gone pretty much as expected, but despite being very […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive back Nick Whiteside (38) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions have banked three training camp practices so far in 2026, and after a day off on Saturday, they’ll stack another six practices in consecutive days while welcoming fans into their Allen Park training facility starting on Sunday. For the most part, things have gone pretty much as expected, but despite being very early in camp, there have been a few surprises (both good and bad) that have resulted from unexpected performances/circumstances. Here are a few examples that have stood out to me. Blake Miller essentially locking up the RT spot from the jump Jahmyr Gibbs holding out for a new contract Sione Vaki getting RB1 snaps UDFA rookie Miles Kitselman running with the first-team as TE3 Tyler Lacy continuing to start at Big End Ahmed Hassanein’s transformation has led to more opportunities Jimmy Rolder taking on the second-team MIKE role Ennis Rakestraw and Rock Ya-Sin splitting starting CB reps Avonte Maddox and Chuck Clark starting at safety over Thomas Harper Greg Dortch looks like the leader for BOTH returner roles Which leans us to today’s question of the day: Which Lions player has been the biggest surprise in camp? My answer : CB Nick Whiteside leveling up his game. On Day one of training camp, Whiteside was arguably the most impactful player on the field, forcing three pass breakups while showing great range and closing burst in coverage. “He’s improved,” coach Dan Campbell said at the following morning’s press conferecne. “And what you like about Ironsides (Whiteside) is that when we brought him in, gave him an opportunity, he fought, made some plays, man earned the right to stay, pulled him up, needed him, did some good things for us. We get him back with us here and look, he’s all about business. It’s not too big for him, he’s all about business and he’s going to maximize everything he’s got. And he looks like he wants a spot and he wants a job, that’s what he looks like. I mean, I know it’s day one, but he made more plays than anybody out there. So that’s encouraging, it’s good to see.” On Day 3, Whiteside managed to not only break up a pass during practice, but he also hauled in an interception as well . While it’s still very early in camp, and we should be cautious in getting over excited, making five impactful plays through just three days of camp is noteworthy. At this time, I feel pretty solid about my CB rankings, but Whiteside’s performance has me wondering if I could make room for him on my next 53-man roster projection. So what do you think? title: The Packers believe they’re contenders
summary: I spent a lot of time this offseason writing about national takes on the Packers’ offseason. There seems to have been a consensus among national writers, or at least among the national takesmiths, that the Packers’ offseason was a disaster. I read numerous pieces about how much talent the Packers had lost, how they failed […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JUNE 09: Head coach Matt LaFleur talks with the media before the Green Bay Packers mandatory minicamp at Don Hutson Center on June 09, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images I spent a lot of time this offseason writing about national takes on the Packers’ offseason. There seems to have been a consensus among national writers, or at least among the national takesmiths, that the Packers’ offseason was a disaster. I read numerous pieces about how much talent the Packers had lost, how they failed to replace it, and how that means they’re sunk for this coming year. Most of that seems flatly untrue, or at least possible to defeat as an argument by just saying “we’ll see.” Because that’s always the case, isn’t it? Nobody really knows how anyone’s offseason has gone until we see the results on the field, and we won’t see those results for months yet. Did the Packers really have a bad offseason? Well, I guess we’ll see. But that criticism aside, I think the Packers had exactly the offseason they wanted to have, more or less. Which is to say, they had an offseason that supports their belief that they were prepared to compete for a Super Bowl last year and they’re expecting to do the same this year. You know the story of the Packers’ 2025 season. It fell apart down the stretch as the team itself seemed to disintegrate. The injury list speaks for itself: Tucker Kraft, Micah Parsons, and Zach Tom, are just the headlines, but plenty of other players were dinged up or lost entirely as the season wore on, and all that culminated in the Packers’ shorthanded loss to the Bears in the wildcard round. To hear national writers tell it, the Packers responded to that reality by jettisoning half their team. But if you paid any kind of attention, you could easily see the plan behind their moves. The Packers cut ties with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks because the “no number one receivers” era was over; they wanted to trim down their wide receiver room and did so by giving extensions to their two most explosive pass catchers and clearing the way for their 2025 first round pick to take on a bigger role. They moved on from Elgton Jenkins because he was old and injured and expensive and disgruntled after spending a year lightly grousing about his position switch. Wouldn’t you have done the same? They traded Rashan Gary because the Cowboys were willing to give them a fourth round pick for a player who (how to say this gently?) rode Micah Parsons’ coat tails for half a season and then disappeared entirely after Parsons went down. They let Quay Walker head to Las Vegas because he was a poor fit for their defensive philosophy. Walker even said as much (though in a bit more of a complaint-oriented fashion) in his introductory press conference with the Raiders, talking obtusely about his poor fit and usage in Green Bay. And they cut Nate Hobbs because he was rarely healthy last year and was bad when he was. It’s not any more complicated than that, and we need not pretend otherwise. Even when he was healthy, he only cracked 20 snaps in a game once after Week 7, and that was for a Packers’ team whose secondary was often the main culprit in late-game collapses. To account for these losses, the Packers are banking on their 2026 first round pick, which they flipped to the Cowboys last year for Micah Parsons. I know I’m playing a bit fast and loose here, but really, it’s not fair to count the Packers’ lack of a first round pick this spring against them if they already used that first round pick to acquire Parsons. What are the odds you’re going to land a Hall of Fame-track player in the late first round, anyway? Surely that should factor into an assessment of their offseason, right? Yet it rarely seems to. More to the point, the Packers will rely on draft picks Brandon Cisse, Chris McClellan, and (to a lesser extent) Dani Dennis-Sutton to make up for whatever deficiencies the defense had last year, in addition to the services of free agent signings Javon Hargrave and Benjamin St-Juste. All of these moves directly address weaknesses the Packers had last year, and all fit with the overall plan of remaining contenders for this season. The Packers essentially operated exactly as you’d expect this offseason. Yes, it was quiet. So what? They cut dead wood, shored up weaknesses as they could, and refined and refocused their offensive approach. They’re clearly sending the message that they know what went wrong last year: their team fell apart at the most critical points, and they’ve added talent to compensate. Will it work? I’d say we’ll see, but that would put me behind everyone decrying their offseason with certainty. Instead, how about we say it looks like they’re headed in the right direction: right back to contender status — which is where they believed they’d be all along.

title: Irsay-Gordon believes the Colts have all they need to win
summary: Carlie Irsay-Gordon is leading the way for the Indianapolis Colts. Yes, she shares ownership with her sisters, but she is calling the shots at the highest level. The late Jim Irsay wasn’t afraid of labeling a season or issuing an “all chips in” type of claim, and it appears that neither is Irsay-Gordon. “Find a […]
full_text: Carlie Irsay-Gordon is leading the way for the Indianapolis Colts. Yes, she shares ownership with her sisters, but she is calling the shots at the highest level. The late Jim Irsay wasn’t afraid of labeling a season or issuing an “all chips in” type of claim, and it appears that neither is Irsay-Gordon. “Find a Way” is this year’s theme, which means there is no room for excuses. At training camp in Westfield, she reiterated her faith in Chris Ballard and Shane Steichen. And why wouldn’t she? It was her decision to bring them back, and she isn’t going to shy away from that before the season starts. Irsay-Gordon also stated that she feels the Colts have everything they need to be successful. If ownership says you have what you need and to find a way to win and you fall short, the consequence will be severe. Leadership doesn’t equip its team with the tools and assets to win only to tolerate failure. At the end of the day, what would the excuse be? She feels the GM, coach, and quarterback are all set up for success. If this season is fumbled, there will be no one left to blame. Is her sentiment correct or fair? That is debatable. Some fans may see a flawed product in this year’s team, but only one opinion matters. That woman believes the Colts have what it takes, so Ballard and Steichen better deliver. Maybe Carlie Irsay-Gordon is simply speaking candidly. Maybe she is sending a subtle message. Maybe she is doing both. Whatever she means, it sounds like excuses won’t be accepted this year. Whatever occurs, the Colts must find a way to win. That’s it. Find a way, or Ballard, Steichen, and anyone else who falls short will find themselves seeking new employment.
